name: Base-catalyzed Aldol addition
text: Hidden event (enolate), seen in Base-catalyzed Aldol addition. Trigger: Carbonyl compound containing an alpha-hydrogen treated with a base Role: Acts as a carbon nucleophile, attacking an electrophilic carbonyl group to forge a new carbon-carbon bond Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])=C[O-]

name: Base-catalyzed Aldol addition
text: Hidden event (alkoxide), seen in Base-catalyzed Aldol addition. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a carbon nucleophile (such as an enolate) to a carbonyl group Role: Abstracts a proton from the conjugate acid or solvent to afford the neutral beta-hydroxy carbonyl product Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])C([O-])C([*:1])([*:2])C=O

name: Acid-catalyzed Aldol addition
text: Hidden event (enol), seen in Acid-catalyzed Aldol addition. Trigger: Carbonyl compound possessing an alpha-hydrogen in the presence of an acid catalyst Role: Acts as a carbon nucleophile, using its C=C pi electrons to attack an activated carbonyl electrophile and form the key C-C bond Example intermediate: C(=C[*:2])(O)[*:1]

name: Acyoin Condensation
text: Hidden event (enediolate dianion), seen in Acyoin Condensation. Trigger: A 1,2-diketone exposed to an alkali metal reducing agent in an aprotic solvent. Role: Resists further reduction due to electrostatic repulsion, preserving the oxidation level until workup where protonation and tautomerization deliver the alpha-hydroxy ketone. Example intermediate: [O-]C([*:1])=C([O-])[*:1]

name: Acyoin Condensation
text: Hidden event (1,2-diketone), seen in Acyoin Condensation. Trigger: Expulsion of two alkoxide leaving groups from a vicinal bis(tetrahedral) pinacolate-like dianion. Role: Acts as an easily reducible electrophilic intermediate that undergoes rapid two-electron reduction by the alkali metal faster than the starting ester, driving the condensation forward. Example intermediate: O=C([*:1])C(=O)[*:1]

name: Acyoin Condensation
text: Hidden event (ketyl radical anion), seen in Acyoin Condensation. Trigger: An ester carbonyl group subjected to a single-electron transfer from a strongly reducing alkali metal. Role: Undergoes radical-radical homocoupling to forge the key carbon-carbon bond connecting the two ester fragments. Example intermediate: [C]([O-])([*:1])(O[*:2])

name: Base-catalyzed Aldol condensation

name: Base-catalyzed Aldol condensation
text: Hidden event (alkoxide intermediate), seen in Base-catalyzed Aldol condensation. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of an enolate to an aldehyde or ketone carbonyl group Role: Undergoes protonation to form a neutral beta-hydroxy carbonyl intermediate Example intermediate: C([*:2])([*:3])([O-])C(C=O)[*:1]

name: Base-catalyzed Aldol condensation
text: Hidden event (enolate intermediate), seen in Base-catalyzed Aldol condensation. Trigger: Deprotonation at the alpha-position of a carbonyl compound bearing a beta-leaving group under basic conditions Role: Expels the beta-hydroxy leaving group via an E1cB pathway to forge the conjugated alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl product Example intermediate: C([*:2])([*:3])(O)C=C([O-])[*:1]

name: Base-catalyzed Aldol condensation

name: Base-catalyzed Aldol condensation
text: Hidden event (enolate intermediate), seen in Base-catalyzed Aldol condensation. Trigger: Deprotonation at the alpha-position of a carbonyl compound bearing a beta-leaving group under basic conditions Role: Expels the beta-hydroxy leaving group via an E1cB pathway to forge the conjugated alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl product Example intermediate: C([*:2])([*:3])(O)C=C([O-])[*:1]

name: Acid-catalyzed Aldol condensation
text: Hidden event (aldol adduct), seen in Acid-catalyzed Aldol condensation. Trigger: Acid- or base-catalyzed nucleophilic addition of an enol or enolate to an aldehyde or ketone carbonyl group. Role: Serves as the pivotal addition intermediate that undergoes dehydration via protonation of the beta-hydroxyl group and elimination to furnish the conjugated alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl product. Example intermediate: C([*:2])([*:3])(O)C(C=O)[*:1]

name: Acid-catalyzed Aldol condensation
text: Hidden event (enol), seen in Acid-catalyzed Aldol condensation. Trigger: A carbonyl compound possessing at least one alpha-hydrogen in the presence of an acid catalyst undergoes keto-enol tautomerization. Role: Acts as a neutral carbon nucleophile that attacks an activated (protonated) carbonyl electrophile to form the new carbon-carbon bond. Example intermediate: C([*:1])=C(O)[*:2]

name: Alkyne zipper reaction
text: Hidden event (propargylic/allenic carbanion), seen in Alkyne zipper reaction. Trigger: Deprotonation of a propargylic C-H bond adjacent to an alkyne or allene by a strong base Role: Delocalizes electron density between the alkyne and allene positions, enabling protonation at the opposite terminus to migrate the unsaturation along the carbon skeleton Example intermediate: [*:1]C#C[CH-]C

name: Alkyne zipper reaction
text: Hidden event (alkynyl carbanion), seen in Alkyne zipper reaction. Trigger: Deprotonation of a newly formed terminal alkyne by strong base under basic isomerization conditions Role: Acts as the thermodynamic sink of the isomerization cascade, locking the unsaturation at the chain terminus until workup Example intermediate: [*:1]CCC#[C-]

name: Alkyne zipper reaction
text: Hidden event (allene intermediate), seen in Alkyne zipper reaction. Trigger: Protonation of a delocalized propargylic/allenic carbanion at the propargylic terminus under isomerization conditions Role: Serves as a transient relay species that is readily deprotonated again to continue walking the unsaturation toward the terminus Example intermediate: [*:1]C=C=CC

name: Appel reaction
text: Hidden event (alkoxyphosphonium intermediate), seen in Appel reaction. Trigger: attack of an alcohol or alkoxide oxygen on an electrophilic halophosphonium species Role: activates the hydroxyl-bearing carbon toward nucleophilic substitution by serving as an excellent leaving group, driven by the thermodynamic stability of the phosphine oxide byproduct Example intermediate: [P+](OC([*:1])([*:2])([*:3]))(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: Appel reaction
text: Hidden event (halophosphonium intermediate), seen in Appel reaction. Trigger: halophilic attack of a triaryl- or trialkylphosphine on a tetrahalomethane or elemental halogen Role: acts as an electrophilic phosphorus center that captures the alcohol substrate while liberating a halide ion to serve as the nucleophile Example intermediate: [P+](c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)Br

name: Appel reaction
text: Hidden event (trihalomethyl carbanion), seen in Appel reaction. Trigger: halophilic cleavage of a carbon-halogen bond in a tetrahalomethane by a neutral nucleophile such as a tertiary phosphine Role: functions as a strong Brønsted base that deprotonates the alcohol substrate into a nucleophilic alkoxide Example intermediate: [C-](Br)(Br)Br

name: Baeyer-Villiger oxidation
text: Hidden event (peroxyhemiacetal intermediate), seen in Baeyer-Villiger oxidation. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a peroxycarboxylic acid (or hydroperoxide) to an activated carbonyl group under acidic or neutral conditions. Role: Undergoes a concerted 1,2-alkyl or aryl migration to the adjacent peroxy oxygen atom with concomitant cleavage of the weak O–O bond, expelling a carboxylate leaving group and driving the rearrangement to the ester. Example intermediate: C([*:1])([OH])(OOC(=O)[*:3])[*:2]

name: Baker-Venkataraman rearrangement
text: Hidden event (cyclic tetrahedral intermediate), seen in Baker-Venkataraman rearrangement. Trigger: Intramolecular nucleophilic attack of an enolate onto a tethered ester carbonyl under basic conditions Role: Collapses by reforming the carbonyl pi bond and cleaving the endocyclic carbon-oxygen bond to release a phenoxide leaving group, completing acyl transfer Example intermediate: c12c(cccc1)OC([O-])([*:3])C([*:1])([*:2])C2=O

name: Bamford-Stevens Reaction
text: Hidden event (carbene), seen in Bamford-Stevens Reaction. Trigger: Thermal or spontaneous extrusion of dinitrogen (N2) from a diazoalkane intermediate Role: Undergoes a rapid 1,2-hydride or 1,2-alkyl shift to furnish the alkene product Example intermediate: [C](C([*:1])([*:2]))([*:3])

name: Bamford-Stevens Reaction
text: Hidden event (diazoalkane), seen in Bamford-Stevens Reaction. Trigger: Base-promoted elimination of an arylsulfinate leaving group from a deprotonated N-sulfonylhydrazone Role: Loses dinitrogen as a leaving group to generate a reactive divalent carbon species Example intermediate: C(=[N+]=[N-])(C([*:1])([*:2]))([*:3])

name: Büchner-Curtius-Schlotterbeck Reaction
text: Hidden event (beta-diazonium alkoxide), seen in Büchner-Curtius-Schlotterbeck Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a diazoalkane (such as diazomethane) to an aldehyde or ketone carbonyl group Role: Re-formation of the carbonyl C=O double bond promotes a 1,2-alkyl or hydride migration onto the adjacent carbon, expelling dinitrogen as a leaving group to yield the homologated carbonyl compound Example intermediate: C([O-])(C[N+]#N)([*:1])([*:2])

name: Buchner Ring Expansion
text: Hidden event (norcaradiene intermediate), seen in Buchner Ring Expansion. Trigger: Addition of a carbene or metal carbenoid across a formal C=C double bond of an aromatic ring under thermal, photochemical, or metal-catalyzed conditions Role: Relieves cyclopropane ring strain by undergoing a disrotatory 6π electrocyclic ring opening to afford the expanded cycloheptatriene core Example intermediate: C(C(=O)[*:1])1C([*:2])2C([*:3])=C([*:4])C([*:5])=C([*:6])C2([*:7])1

name: Buchner Ring Expansion
text: Hidden event (carbene intermediate), seen in Buchner Ring Expansion. Trigger: Loss of dinitrogen from an α-diazocarbonyl compound initiated by heat, light, or transition-metal catalysis Role: Acts as an electrophilic divalent carbon species that undergoes [2+1] cycloaddition with an arene double bond Example intermediate: [CH]C(=O)[*:1]

name: Burgess Dehydration
text: Hidden event (alkyl sulfamate inner salt), seen in Burgess Dehydration. Trigger: Reaction of an alcohol bearing a beta-hydrogen with an electrophilic sulfamoyl carbamate reagent (e.g., the Burgess reagent) via nucleophilic displacement of a tertiary amine and subsequent deprotonation. Role: Undergoes a concerted, cyclic syn-elimination (Ei mechanism) wherein the tethered carbamate nitrogen acts as an intramolecular base to abstract the beta-hydrogen with simultaneous cleavage of the C-O bond, delivering an alkene. Example intermediate: COC(=O)[N-]S(=O)(=O)OC([*:1])([*:2])C([*:3])([*:4])

name: Cadogan-Sundberg Indole Synthesis
text: Hidden event (nitrosoarene), seen in Cadogan-Sundberg Indole Synthesis. Trigger: A nitroarene heated in the presence of an oxophilic trivalent phosphorus reagent (such as a trialkyl phosphite or triarylphosphine) Role: Acts as a reactive intermediate that undergoes intramolecular cyclization onto the adjacent ortho-alkenyl substituent to construct the pyrrole ring Example intermediate: c1(C([*:2])=C([*:3]))c(N=O)cc([*:1])cc1

name: Cadogan-Sundberg Indole Synthesis
text: Hidden event (heteroaromatic N-oxide), seen in Cadogan-Sundberg Indole Synthesis. Trigger: Intramolecular attack or cyclization of an ortho-alkenyl nitrosoarene onto the pendant alkene moiety Role: Forms the bicyclic indole skeleton and undergoes a subsequent deoxygenation by phosphorus(III) to generate the aromatic indole core Example intermediate: c1c([*:1])cc2c(n([O-])c([*:3])c2[*:2])c1

name: Cadogan-Sundberg Indole Synthesis
text: Hidden event (phosphonium betaine), seen in Cadogan-Sundberg Indole Synthesis. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a phosphorus(III) reagent (e.g., phosphite or phosphine) to an oxygen atom of an aromatic nitro group Role: Facilitates net deoxygenation of the nitro group via extrusion of the corresponding phosphine oxide or phosphate ester Example intermediate: c1(C([*:2])=C([*:3]))c(N([O-])([O][P+]([*:4])([*:4])[*:4]))cc([*:1])cc1

name: Corey-Fuchs Reaction
text: Hidden event (oxaphosphetane), seen in Corey-Fuchs Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a phosphorus ylide to a carbonyl group followed by formal intramolecular P-O bond formation Role: Collapses via retro-[2+2] cycloelimination to drive the formation of an alkene with irreversible extrusion of a phosphine oxide Example intermediate: O1C([*:1])C(Br)(Br)P1(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: Corey-Fuchs Reaction
text: Hidden event (phosphorus ylide), seen in Corey-Fuchs Reaction. Trigger: Reaction of a triarylphosphine with a tetrahalomethane to form a halophosphonium salt followed by halide-promoted dehalogenation Role: Acts as a carbon nucleophile that attacks the carbonyl group to initiate Wittig-type olefination Example intermediate: BrC(Br)=[P](c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: Corey-Fuchs Reaction
text: Hidden event (haloalkyne), seen in Corey-Fuchs Reaction. Trigger: Base-induced deprotonation of a 1,1-dihaloalkene followed by beta-elimination of a halide leaving group Role: Undergoes rapid lithium-halogen exchange with an alkyllithium reagent to forge an alkynyllithium species Example intermediate: [*:1]C#CBr

name: Corey-Kim Oxidation
text: Hidden event (alkoxysulfonium ion), seen in Corey-Kim Oxidation. Trigger: Nucleophilic attack of an alcohol oxygen onto an electrophilic halosulfonium species, followed by loss of the proton on oxygen Role: Serves as the key activated substrate-reagent adduct that undergoes base-mediated elimination to form the carbonyl product and displace a dialkyl sulfide Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])(H)O[S+](C)C

name: Corey-Kim Oxidation
text: Hidden event (chlorosulfonium ion), seen in Corey-Kim Oxidation. Trigger: Electrophilic chlorination of a dialkyl sulfide by an N-chloroimide such as N-chlorosuccinimide Role: Acts as an activated sulfur electrophile that undergoes nucleophilic displacement by an alcohol to generate an alkoxysulfonium species Example intermediate: S(Cl)(C)C

name: Corey-Nicolaou Macrolactonization
text: Hidden event (acyloxyphosphonium intermediate), seen in Corey-Nicolaou Macrolactonization. Trigger: Attack of a carboxylic acid or carboxylate on an electrophilic phosphonium center, displacing a leaving group such as a thiolate or halide. Role: Greatly enhances the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon toward nucleophilic attack by alcohols, driven by the thermodynamic stability of the phosphine oxide byproduct. Example intermediate: [*:1]C(=O)O[P+](c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)

name: Corey-Nicolaou Macrolactonization
text: Hidden event (tetrahedral intermediate), seen in Corey-Nicolaou Macrolactonization. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a hydroxyl group (alcohol) to the activated carbonyl carbon of an acyloxyphosphonium ion. Role: Collapses via elimination of triphenylphosphine oxide to forge the ester or lactone C-O bond. Example intermediate: [*:1]C([O-])(O([*:2]))O[P+](c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)

name: Corey-Nicolaou Macrolactonization
text: Hidden event (thiophosphonium intermediate), seen in Corey-Nicolaou Macrolactonization. Trigger: Nucleophilic attack of a triarylphosphine on the sulfur-sulfur bond of a diaryl disulfide (such as 2,2'-dipyridyl disulfide). Role: Serves as an activated electrophilic phosphorus center that is trapped by a carboxylic acid to form the acyloxyphosphonium species. Example intermediate: [P+](c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)Sc1ncccc1

name: Corey-Seebach Reaction
text: Hidden event (dithianyl anion), seen in Corey-Seebach Reaction. Trigger: Deprotonation of a 1,3-dithiane or dithioacetal C-H bond flanked by two sulfur atoms using a strong organolithium base (such as n-butyllithium) in an aprotic solvent at low temperature Role: Acts as an umpolung nucleophile (masked acyl anion equivalent) that attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon of an aldehyde or ketone to form a new carbon-carbon bond Example intermediate: S([*:1])[C-]([*:2])S([*:1])

name: Dakin Oxidation
text: Hidden event (tetrahedral peroxy adduct), seen in Dakin Oxidation. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of hydrogen peroxide or hydroperoxide anion to a carbonyl group under basic conditions Role: Undergoes a 1,2-shift (aryl migration) onto the adjacent peroxide oxygen with concerted heterolytic cleavage of the weak O-O bond Example intermediate: [O-][CH](OO)c1c([*:1])cc([*:2])c([*:3])c1([*:4])

name: Dakin Oxidation
text: Hidden event (aryl formate ester), seen in Dakin Oxidation. Trigger: 1,2-migration of an electron-rich aryl group to peroxide oxygen with expulsion of hydroxide from a peroxyalkoxide Role: Serves as an electrophilic acyl intermediate that undergoes rapid nucleophilic addition by hydroxide, enabling subsequent hydrolysis to the phenol Example intermediate: O=COc1c([*:1])cc([*:2])c([*:3])c1([*:4])

name: Dakin Oxidation
text: Hidden event (tetrahedral intermediate), seen in Dakin Oxidation. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of hydroxide to an ester carbonyl under basic aqueous conditions Role: Eliminates the phenoxide leaving group upon reforming the carbonyl pi-bond, completing the saponification of the ester Example intermediate: [O-][CH](O)Oc1c([*:1])cc([*:2])c([*:3])c1([*:4])

name: Dakin-West Reaction
text: Hidden event (mixed anhydride), seen in Dakin-West Reaction. Trigger: A carboxylic acid (or carboxylate) reacting with an acid anhydride in the presence of a mild base such as a tertiary amine. Role: Serves as an activated carboxylic acid derivative that acidifies the alpha-protons, facilitating enolization and subsequent C-acylation. Example intermediate: [CH]([*:1])([*:2])C(=O)OC(=O)C([*:3])

name: Dakin-West Reaction
text: Hidden event (enolate), seen in Dakin-West Reaction. Trigger: Deprotonation of an activated carbonyl compound (such as a mixed anhydride) bearing an alpha-hydrogen by a base. Role: Acts as a carbon nucleophile that attacks an electrophilic carbonyl (an acid anhydride) to forge the new carbon-carbon bond. Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])=C([O-])OC(=O)C([*:3])

name: Dakin-West Reaction
text: Hidden event (beta-keto carboxylate), seen in Dakin-West Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic cleavage of a beta-keto mixed anhydride by carboxylate, unmasking a carboxylate group situated beta to a ketone carbonyl. Role: Undergoes facile decarboxylation via heterolytic C-C bond cleavage to release carbon dioxide and drive the reaction forward. Example intermediate: C([*:3])C(=O)C([*:1])([*:2])C(=O)[O-]

name: Danheiser Benzannulation
text: Hidden event (dienylketene), seen in Danheiser Benzannulation. Trigger: Thermal 4π electrocyclic ring opening of a 4-alkenylcyclobutenone Role: Undergoes 6π electrocyclization to form a 2,4-cyclohexadienone ring, constructing the six-membered carbocycle Example intermediate: C([*:5])=C([*:1])C([*:2])=C(EDG)C([*:4])=C=O

name: Danheiser Benzannulation
text: Hidden event (4-alkenylcyclobutenone), seen in Danheiser Benzannulation. Trigger: Thermal [2+2] cycloaddition between a vinylketene and an alkyne Role: Undergoes thermal 4π electrocyclic ring opening to release ring strain and generate the reactive dienylketene intermediate Example intermediate: C([*:5])=C([*:1])C1([*:2])C(=O)C([*:4])=C1(EDG)

name: Danheiser Benzannulation
text: Hidden event (vinylketene), seen in Danheiser Benzannulation. Trigger: Thermal 4π electrocyclic ring opening of a cyclobutenone Role: Traps an alkyne via [2+2] cycloaddition to assemble the 4-alkenylcyclobutenone scaffold Example intermediate: C([*:5])=C([*:1])C([*:2])=C=O

name: De Mayo Reaction
text: Hidden event (cyclobutanol), seen in De Mayo Reaction. Trigger: Photochemical [2+2] cycloaddition between an enol (such as that of a 1,3-dicarbonyl compound) and an alkene under UV irradiation Role: Undergoes retro-aldol fragmentation driven by the relief of cyclobutane ring strain to yield the 1,5-dicarbonyl product Example intermediate: O=C([*:1])C([*:2])C1(O)C([*:3])C1([*:4])([*:5])([*:6])

name: Dess-Martin Oxidation
text: Hidden event (alkoxyperiodinane adduct), seen in Dess-Martin Oxidation. Trigger: Ligand exchange of an alcohol onto a hypervalent iodine(V) reagent (such as Dess-Martin periodinane) with displacement of an acetate ligand under mild, aprotic conditions. Role: Covalently activates the alcohol oxygen, positioning the alpha C-H bond for base-assisted elimination and concomitant two-electron reduction of iodine(V) to iodine(III) to generate the carbonyl product. Example intermediate: CC(=O)OI1(OC(=O)C)(OC([H])([*:1])[*:2])C2=CC=CC=C2C(=O)O1

name: Dieckmann Condensation
text: Hidden event (tetrahedral intermediate), seen in Dieckmann Condensation. Trigger: Intramolecular nucleophilic attack of an enolate carbon onto an ester carbonyl group under basic conditions Role: Collapses by reforming the carbonyl pi bond and expelling an alkoxide leaving group to give the cyclic beta-keto ester Example intermediate: O([*:1])C(=O)C1C([O-])(O([*:2]))CCC1

name: Dieckmann Condensation
text: Hidden event (ester enolate), seen in Dieckmann Condensation. Trigger: Deprotonation of the alpha-carbon of an ester containing acidic alpha-hydrogens by base Role: Serves as a resonance-stabilized carbon nucleophile that attacks the electrophilic ester carbonyl to form a ring Example intermediate: O([*:1])C(=O)[CH-]CCCC(=O)O([*:2])

name: Doebner-Miller Reaction
text: Hidden event (1,2-dihydroquinoline), seen in Doebner-Miller Reaction. Trigger: Acid-catalyzed elimination of water (dehydration) from a 4-hydroxytetrahydroquinoline intermediate Role: Acts as the key non-aromatic bicyclic intermediate that undergoes oxidation/dehydrogenation to yield the fully aromatic quinoline product Example intermediate: C1([*:5])C(([*:6]))=C(([*:7]))C2=C(N1)c(([*:4]))c(([*:2]))c(([*:1]))c2([*:3])

name: Doebner-Miller Reaction
text: Hidden event (beta-amino carbonyl adduct), seen in Doebner-Miller Reaction. Trigger: Conjugate (Michael) addition of an arylamine to an alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl compound under acidic conditions Role: Covalently links the amine to the three-carbon unit, positioning the carbonyl for subsequent intramolecular cyclization onto the aromatic ring Example intermediate: C([*:7])(=O)C(([*:6]))C(([*:5]))Nc1cc(([*:3]))c(([*:1]))c(([*:2]))c1([*:4])

name: Doebner-Miller Reaction
text: Hidden event (4-hydroxy-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroquinoline), seen in Doebner-Miller Reaction. Trigger: Intramolecular electrophilic aromatic substitution (Friedel-Crafts-type cyclization) of an aniline ring onto an activated tethered carbonyl Role: Forms the carbocyclic/heterocyclic fused bicyclic framework and serves as the precursor for acid-mediated dehydration Example intermediate: C1([*:5])C(([*:6]))C([OH])(([*:7]))C2=C(N1)c(([*:4]))c(([*:2]))c(([*:1]))c2([*:3])

name: Evans-Mislow Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (allyl sulfenate ester), seen in Evans-Mislow Rearrangement. Trigger: An allylic sulfoxide subjected to thermal or ambient conditions, undergoing a reversible [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement Role: Trapped irreversibly via nucleophilic attack at sulfur by a thiophilic reagent (such as a trialkyl phosphite), cleaving the S-O bond and driving the equilibrium toward the allylic alcohol product Example intermediate: S([*:6])OC([*:1])([*:2])C([*:3])=C([*:4])([*:5])

name: Favorskii Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (cyclopropanone intermediate), seen in Favorskii Rearrangement. Trigger: Ketone bearing a leaving group (such as a halogen) at one alpha position and a hydrogen atom at the opposing alpha position, under basic conditions facilitating enolization and intramolecular substitution. Role: Acts as a highly strained electrophilic intermediate that undergoes rapid nucleophilic addition to its carbonyl group, setting up subsequent ring-opening rearrangement. Example intermediate: O=C1C2([*:3])CCCCC([*:1])([*:2])C12

name: Favorskii Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (carbanion intermediate), seen in Favorskii Rearrangement. Trigger: Collapse of a cyclopropanoxide oxyanion, where relief of cyclopropane ring strain promotes endocyclic C-C bond cleavage. Role: Directs the regiochemical outcome of the skeletal rearrangement by preferentially forming the more stable carbanion, which is then protonated by a protic solvent to yield the final carboxylic acid derivative. Example intermediate: [*:5]OC(=O)C1([*:1])([*:2])CCCC[C-]1([*:3])

name: Favorskii Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (tetrahedral intermediate), seen in Favorskii Rearrangement. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of an alkoxide or hydroxide to the carbonyl carbon of a strained cyclopropanone. Role: Re-forms the carbonyl C=O bond via oxyanion collapse, expelling a ring carbon atom as a leaving group to relieve cyclopropane ring strain. Example intermediate: [O-]C1(O([*:5]))C2([*:3])CCCCC([*:1])([*:2])C12

name: Fritsch-Buttenberg-Wiechell Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (alkylidene carbene), seen in Fritsch-Buttenberg-Wiechell Rearrangement. Trigger: alpha-elimination of a halide or other leaving group from an alpha-haloalkenyl anion under strongly basic conditions Role: undergoes a rapid 1,2-shift of an adjacent substituent into the electron-deficient carbene center to generate an alkyne Example intermediate: C(=[C])([*:1])([*:2])

name: Fritsch-Buttenberg-Wiechell Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (alpha-haloalkenyl carbanion), seen in Fritsch-Buttenberg-Wiechell Rearrangement. Trigger: deprotonation of a 1-haloalkene at the vinyl C-H position using a strong, non-nucleophilic base (e.g., LDA or organolithium) Role: acts as a carbenoid intermediate that expels the halide leaving group to deliver a reactive alkylidene carbene Example intermediate: C(=[C-]Br)([*:1])([*:2])

name: Fries Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (acylium ion), seen in Fries Rearrangement. Trigger: Heterolytic cleavage of an acyl-heteroatom bond promoted by coordination to a strong Lewis acid Role: Serves as the key reactive electrophile that undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution onto the electron-rich arene Example intermediate: [O+]#C[*:4]

name: Fries Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (arenium ion), seen in Fries Rearrangement. Trigger: Electrophilic addition of a strong cation to an aromatic ring, temporarily disrupting aromaticity Role: Acts as a high-energy intermediate that rapidly loses a proton to re-aromatize and establish the new carbon-carbon bond Example intermediate: C(=O)([*:4])C1=C(O[Al-](Cl)(Cl)Cl)C([*:1])=C([*:2])C=C1([*:3])

name: Fries Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (Lewis acid-carbonyl adduct), seen in Fries Rearrangement. Trigger: Coordination of a carbonyl oxygen lone pair to a strong Lewis acid with an open coordination site Role: Strongly polarizes the acyl group and weakens the acyl-oxygen bond, driving the formation of the acylium ion Example intermediate: c1(OC(=[O+][Al-](Cl)(Cl)Cl)[*:4])c([*:1])c([*:2])cc([*:3])c1

name: Fujimoto-Belleau Reaction
text: Hidden event (tetrahedral intermediate), seen in Fujimoto-Belleau Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a carbon nucleophile (such as a Grignard or organolithium reagent) to an ester or lactone carbonyl group. Role: Collapses with cleavage of the endocyclic C-O bond to effect ring-opening and generate a keto-enolate intermediate. Example intermediate: C1CC(C[*:1])([O-])OC2=C([*:2])CCCC12

name: Fujimoto-Belleau Reaction
text: Hidden event (aldol adduct), seen in Fujimoto-Belleau Reaction. Trigger: Intramolecular nucleophilic addition of an enolate carbon onto a tethered carbonyl group within a dicarbonyl framework. Role: Forms the new carbocyclic ring and undergoes subsequent dehydration to furnish the conjugated bicyclic enone. Example intermediate: C1CC(=O)C([*:1])C2([O-])C([*:2])CCCC12

name: Fujimoto-Belleau Reaction
text: Hidden event (enolate intermediate), seen in Fujimoto-Belleau Reaction. Trigger: Collapse of a cyclic tetrahedral intermediate derived from an enol lactone, expelling the enolic oxygen. Role: Undergoes tautomeric proton transfer to reposition the enolate for downstream regioselective aldol cyclization. Example intermediate: [O-]C1=C([*:2])CCCC1CCCC(=O)(C[*:1])

name: Ganem Oxidation
text: Hidden event (alkoxyammonium ion), seen in Ganem Oxidation. Trigger: Nucleophilic displacement of a leaving group (such as halide or sulfonate) on an sp3 carbon by the oxygen atom of a tertiary amine N-oxide Role: Acts as an activated electrophilic intermediate bearing a good tertiary amine leaving group on oxygen, enabling rapid alpha-deprotonation/elimination to generate the carbonyl product Example intermediate: C(O[N+](CC)(CC)CC)([*:1])([*:2])

name: Haloform Reaction
text: Hidden event (tetrahedral intermediate), seen in Haloform Reaction. Trigger: Addition of a hydroxide or oxygen nucleophile to a carbonyl group bearing an electron-withdrawing leaving group under basic conditions Role: Collapses by reforming the carbonyl pi bond and expelling a trihalomethyl carbanion, leading to carbon-carbon bond cleavage Example intermediate: C([O-])(O)(C(Br)(Br)Br)[*:1]

name: Haloform Reaction
text: Hidden event (trihalomethyl carbanion), seen in Haloform Reaction. Trigger: C-C bond cleavage upon collapse of a tetrahedral carbonyl addition intermediate bearing a trihalomethyl group Role: Acts as an expelled carbon-centered leaving group and subsequently deprotonates the co-generated carboxylic acid to form haloform and drive the reaction forward Example intermediate: [C-](Br)(Br)Br

name: Hanessian-Hullar Reaction
text: Hidden event (dioxocarbenium ion), seen in Hanessian-Hullar Reaction. Trigger: Expulsion of a halide leaving group from an alpha-halo cyclic acetal, driven by resonance stabilization from adjacent oxygen atoms. Role: Suffers regioselective nucleophilic attack by a halide ion at an alkyl carbon, opening the ring to yield an omega-haloalkyl ester. Example intermediate: [O+]1=C(c2ccccc2)OC([*:1])([*:2])CC1

name: Hanessian-Hullar Reaction
text: Hidden event (alpha-halo acetal), seen in Hanessian-Hullar Reaction. Trigger: Radical halogenation at the acetal (often benzylic) C-H position of a cyclic acetal using reagents like NBS or Br2. Role: Acts as an unstable intermediate that eliminates a halide leaving group to generate a resonance-stabilized cyclic dioxocarbenium ion. Example intermediate: O1C(Br)(c2ccccc2)OC([*:1])([*:2])CC1

name: Hantzsch Thiazole Synthesis
text: Hidden event (cyclic carbinolamine), seen in Hantzsch Thiazole Synthesis. Trigger: Intramolecular nucleophilic addition of a tethered amine or imine nitrogen to a carbonyl group (ketone or aldehyde) during heterocycle condensation Role: Acts as the cyclized precursor that undergoes protonation and irreversible dehydration to drive aromatization to the heteroaromatic ring Example intermediate: [*:1]C1=[NH+]C([*:3])(O)C([*:2])S1

name: Hantzsch Thiazole Synthesis
text: Hidden event (S-alkylated thioimidate), seen in Hantzsch Thiazole Synthesis. Trigger: Nucleophilic displacement of an alpha-halo carbonyl compound by the soft sulfur atom of a thioamide or thiourea derivative Role: Tethers the carbonyl electrophile to the nitrogen-containing fragment, positioning the imine nitrogen for subsequent intramolecular cyclization Example intermediate: C([*:1])(=[NH2+])SC([*:2])C([*:3])(=O)

name: Hass-Bender Oxidation
text: Hidden event (nitronic ester), seen in Hass-Bender Oxidation. Trigger: O-alkylation of a resonance-stabilized nitronate anion by an activated alkyl halide (such as a benzylic or allylic halide) Role: undergoes elimination/fragmentation via cleavage of the weak N-O bond to generate the carbonyl product and an oxime byproduct Example intermediate: [N+]([O-])(=C(C)C)OCc1c([*:1])c([*:2])c([*:3])c([*:4])c1[*:5]

name: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky Reaction
text: Hidden event (acyl halide enol), seen in Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky Reaction. Trigger: An acyl halide bearing an alpha-hydrogen under acidic conditions (such as in the presence of hydrogen halide). Role: Acts as an electron-rich carbon nucleophile that attacks molecular halogen to forge the alpha carbon-halogen bond. Example intermediate: C([*:1])=C([OH])Br

name: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky Reaction
text: Hidden event (acyl halide), seen in Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky Reaction. Trigger: A carboxylic acid treated with a phosphorus halide or elemental phosphorus and halogen. Role: Enolizes vastly more rapidly than the parent carboxylic acid, serving as the necessary precursor to access the reactive enol tautomer. Example intermediate: C([*:1])C(=O)Br

name: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky Reaction
text: Hidden event (O-phosphitylated carboxylic acid), seen in Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic attack of a carboxylic acid oxygen onto an electrophilic phosphorus halide. Role: Converts the poor hydroxyl leaving group into a good phosphorus-based leaving group, enabling subsequent halide displacement to yield the acyl halide. Example intermediate: C([*:1])C(=[O])[OH+]P(Br)Br

name: Hemetsberger-Knittel Indole Synthesis
text: Hidden event (vinyl nitrene), seen in Hemetsberger-Knittel Indole Synthesis. Trigger: Thermal or photochemical decomposition of an alkenyl azide (vinyl azide) via extrusion of molecular nitrogen Role: Undergoes intramolecular 6pi-electrocyclization with an adjacent aromatic ring to forge the C-N bond of the heterocyclic ring Example intermediate: [N]/C(=C/c1c([*:4])c([*:3])c([*:2])c([*:1])c1)\C(=O)O[*:5]

name: Hemetsberger-Knittel Indole Synthesis
text: Hidden event (2H-indole), seen in Hemetsberger-Knittel Indole Synthesis. Trigger: Intramolecular 6pi-electrocyclization of an ortho-aryl vinyl nitrene onto the adjacent aromatic ring Role: Undergoes a suprafacial [1,5]-sigmatropic hydrogen shift from C2 to N1 to rearomatize the ring system to a 1H-indole Example intermediate: [*:5]OC(=O)C1C=C2C(=[n]1)c(c(c(c2[*:4])[*:3])[*:2])[*:1]

name: Henry Reaction
text: Hidden event (nitronate anion), seen in Henry Reaction. Trigger: Nitroalkane possessing an alpha-hydrogen in the presence of a base Role: Acts as a resonance-stabilized carbon nucleophile that attacks a carbonyl electrophile to form a new carbon-carbon bond Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])=[N+]([O-])[O-]

name: Henry Reaction
text: Hidden event (alkoxide intermediate), seen in Henry Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a carbanion or nitronate to an aldehyde or ketone carbonyl group Role: Undergoes protonation to generate the neutral beta-nitroalcohol product and regenerate the base Example intermediate: C([*:3])([*:4])([O-])C([*:1])([*:2])[N+](=O)[O-]

name: Hofmann-Löffler-Freytag Reaction
text: Hidden event (aminyl radical), seen in Hofmann-Löffler-Freytag Reaction. Trigger: Homolytic cleavage of an N-haloamine (N-Cl or N-Br) bond under photochemical irradiation or heating. Role: Undergoes regioselective intramolecular 1,5-hydrogen atom transfer (1,5-HAT) across a six-membered chair-like transition state, translocating the radical to the delta carbon. Example intermediate: [N]([*:3])CCCC([*:1])[*:2]

name: Hofmann-Löffler-Freytag Reaction
text: Hidden event (alkyl radical), seen in Hofmann-Löffler-Freytag Reaction. Trigger: Intramolecular 1,5-hydrogen atom abstraction from a delta-carbon C-H bond by a nitrogen-centered aminyl radical. Role: Abstracts a halogen atom from a precursor N-haloamine molecule to deliver the delta-haloalkylamine product and propagate the radical chain. Example intermediate: N([*:3])CCC[C]([*:1])[*:2]

name: Hofmann Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (isocyanate), seen in Hofmann Rearrangement. Trigger: 1,2-migration of an alkyl or aryl group onto nitrogen with concomitant displacement of a leaving group from an activated acyl nitrogen derivative Role: serves as a reactive electrophilic heterocumulene that is rapidly trapped by nucleophiles such as hydroxide or water to form a carbamic acid derivative Example intermediate: O=C=N[*:1]

name: Hofmann Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (N-haloamide anion), seen in Hofmann Rearrangement. Trigger: deprotonation of an N-haloamide by base, generating an electron-rich conjugate base with a halogen leaving group attached to nitrogen Role: triggers a concerted 1,2-rearrangement with loss of the halide leaving group to form an isocyanate intermediate Example intermediate: C([*:1])(=O)[N-]Br

name: Hofmann Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (carbamate adduct), seen in Hofmann Rearrangement. Trigger: nucleophilic addition of hydroxide or water to the central carbonyl carbon of an isocyanate under aqueous basic conditions Role: undergoes spontaneous decarboxylative fragmentation with extrusion of carbon dioxide (or carbonate) to liberate the primary amine Example intermediate: N(=C(O)[O-])[*:1]

name: Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons Reaction
text: Hidden event (oxaphosphetane), seen in Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons Reaction. Trigger: Intramolecular nucleophilic attack of an oxyanion beta to a phosphoryl group onto the phosphorus atom, forming a four-membered ring intermediate. Role: Undergoes spontaneous retro-[2+2] cycloreversion driven by the formation of a thermodynamic phosphate species to generate the alkene product. Example intermediate: [*:1]OP1([O-])(O[*:1])C([*:2])([*:3])C([*:4])O1

name: Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons Reaction
text: Hidden event (beta-oxidoalkylphosphonate), seen in Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a resonance-stabilized alpha-phosphono carbanion to a carbonyl electrophile. Role: Serves as an acyclic adduct whose alkoxide oxygen attacks the phosphoryl phosphorus to form a four-membered oxaphosphetane. Example intermediate: P(=O)(O[*:1])(O[*:1])C([*:2])([*:3])C([O-])[*:4]

name: Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons Reaction
text: Hidden event (alpha-phosphono carbanion), seen in Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons Reaction. Trigger: Deprotonation of an alkylphosphonate at the alpha-carbon by base, generating a carbanion stabilized by the phosphoryl group. Role: Acts as the carbon nucleophile that attacks the carbonyl carbon to forge the central carbon-carbon bond. Example intermediate: P(=O)(O[*:1])(O[*:1])[C-]([*:2])[*:3]

name: Hosomi-Sakurai Reaction
text: Hidden event (beta-silyl carbocation), seen in Hosomi-Sakurai Reaction. Trigger: Electrophilic addition of an activated carbonyl or other electrophile to an allylsilane, generating a positive charge beta to the silyl group Role: Stabilized by hyperconjugation (the beta-silicon effect), it rapidly undergoes desilylative elimination to regioselectively forge the new carbon-carbon double bond Example intermediate: [Si](C)(C)(C)C([*:1])([*:2])[C+]([*:3])C([*:4])([*:5])C(O[Ti](Cl)(Cl)Cl)([*:6])[*:7]

name: Hosomi-Sakurai Reaction
text: Hidden event (Lewis acid-carbonyl complex), seen in Hosomi-Sakurai Reaction. Trigger: Coordination of a carbonyl oxygen lone pair to a strong Lewis acid Role: Increases the oxocarbenium character and dramatically enhances the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon toward weak pi-nucleophiles Example intermediate: C(=[O+][Ti](Cl)(Cl)Cl)([*:6])[*:7]

name: Hosomi-Sakurai Reaction
text: Hidden event (metal alkoxide), seen in Hosomi-Sakurai Reaction. Trigger: Desilylation and double-bond formation resulting in an alkoxide coordinated to the Lewis acidic metal center Role: Serves as the reagent-bound resting intermediate until protic workup hydrolyzes the oxygen-metal bond to release the alcohol product Example intermediate: C(=C([*:4])[*:5])([*:3])C([*:1])([*:2])C(O[Ti](Cl)(Cl)Cl)([*:6])[*:7]

name: Houben-Hoesch Reaction
text: Hidden event (arenium ion), seen in Houben-Hoesch Reaction. Trigger: Electrophilic attack on an electron-rich aromatic ring by a Lewis acid-activated nitrile, disrupting the aromatic system. Role: Undergoes rearomatization via proton elimination to restore aromaticity, yielding a ketimine. Example intermediate: C1(C(=N[Zn])[*:5])C(=[OH+])c([*:1])c([*:2])c([*:3])c1[*:4]

name: Houben-Hoesch Reaction
text: Hidden event (ketimine), seen in Houben-Hoesch Reaction. Trigger: Rearomatization following electrophilic addition of a nitrile to an electron-rich arene under Lewis acidic conditions. Role: Serves as the key covalent intermediate containing the newly constructed carbon-carbon bond, which undergoes subsequent aqueous acidic hydrolysis to provide the aryl ketone product. Example intermediate: c1(C(=[NH])[*:5])c(O)c([*:1])c([*:2])c([*:3])c1[*:4]

name: Hunsdiecker Reaction
text: Hidden event (acyl hypohalite), seen in Hunsdiecker Reaction. Trigger: Electrophilic halogenation of a carboxylate salt (e.g., silver carboxylate) with molecular halogen Role: Serves as a labile intermediate that undergoes homolytic cleavage of the weak oxygen-halogen bond upon heating or irradiation to initiate a radical cascade Example intermediate: O=C(OBr)[*:1]

name: Hunsdiecker Reaction
text: Hidden event (acyloxy radical), seen in Hunsdiecker Reaction. Trigger: Homolytic cleavage of an acyl hypohalite O-X bond under thermal or photochemical conditions Role: Undergoes rapid and irreversible beta-scission (decarboxylation) releasing carbon dioxide and generating a carbon-centered radical Example intermediate: O=C([O])[*:1]

name: Hunsdiecker Reaction
text: Hidden event (carbon-centered radical), seen in Hunsdiecker Reaction. Trigger: Extrusion of carbon dioxide from an acyloxy radical Role: Abstracts a halogen atom from acyl hypohalite or molecular halogen to yield the haloalkane product and propagate the radical chain Example intermediate: [C]([*:1])

name: Japp-Klingemann Reaction
text: Hidden event (alpha-azo beta-dicarbonyl intermediate), seen in Japp-Klingemann Reaction. Trigger: Coupling of an aryldiazonium salt with the enolate of an alpha-substituted beta-dicarbonyl compound under basic conditions. Role: Because it lacks an alpha-hydrogen, it cannot undergo direct tautomerization to a hydrazone; it instead undergoes nucleophilic attack by hydroxide at the ketone carbonyl to trigger deacylative cleavage. Example intermediate: C(C(=O)O[*:3])(C(=O)[*:1])(N=N[*:4])[*:2]

name: Japp-Klingemann Reaction
text: Hidden event (tetrahedral intermediate), seen in Japp-Klingemann Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of hydroxide to the ketone carbonyl of an alpha-azo beta-dicarbonyl compound under basic aqueous conditions. Role: Collapses to reform the carbonyl pi-bond while expelling the alpha-carbon as a resonance-stabilized hydrazone anion, achieving retro-Claisen C-C cleavage. Example intermediate: C(C(=O)O[*:3])(C(O)([O-])([*:1]))(N=N[*:4])[*:2]

name: Johnson-Claisen Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (allyl vinyl ketene acetal), seen in Johnson-Claisen Rearrangement. Trigger: Condensation of an allylic alcohol with an orthoester under acidic conditions followed by elimination of an alcohol molecule Role: Undergoes a thermal concerted [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement to form a gamma,delta-unsaturated ester Example intermediate: C(=C(OC)C)OC([*:4])([*:5])C([*:3])=C([*:1])[*:2]

name: Johnson-Claisen Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (dialkoxycarbenium ion), seen in Johnson-Claisen Rearrangement. Trigger: Acid-catalyzed ionization of an orthoester via protonation and loss of an alcohol leaving group Role: Functions as a strong electrophile captured by an allylic alcohol to initiate transesterification Example intermediate: [C+](C)(OC)(OC)

name: Johnson-Corey-Chaykovsky Reaction
text: Hidden event (betaine intermediate), seen in Johnson-Corey-Chaykovsky Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a sulfur ylide carbanion to an electrophilic carbonyl group. Role: Undergoes rapid intramolecular substitution where the alkoxide oxygen attacks the adjacent carbon bearing the sulfonium group, expelling a neutral sulfide to forge an epoxide ring. Example intermediate: [O-]C([*:5])([*:6])C([*:3])([*:4])[S+]([*:1])([*:2])

name: Johnson-Corey-Chaykovsky Reaction
text: Hidden event (sulfur ylide), seen in Johnson-Corey-Chaykovsky Reaction. Trigger: Deprotonation of a sulfonium or sulfoxonium salt at the alpha position by a base. Role: Acts as a soft carbanionic nucleophile to attack the electrophilic carbonyl group, initiating the cyclization sequence. Example intermediate: [C-]([*:3])([*:4])[S+]([*:1])([*:2])

name: Jones Oxidation
text: Hidden event (alkyl chromate ester), seen in Jones Oxidation. Trigger: Nucleophilic attack of a primary or secondary alcohol on an electrophilic chromium(VI) species under acidic conditions, followed by deprotonation Role: Undergoes elimination of the alpha-hydrogen with cleavage of the Cr-O bond, reducing Cr(VI) to Cr(IV) and generating a carbonyl group Example intermediate: C([*:1])O[Cr]([O-])(=O)(O)O

name: Jones Oxidation
text: Hidden event (gem-diol), seen in Jones Oxidation. Trigger: Reversible nucleophilic addition of water to an aldehyde under aqueous acidic conditions Role: Provides a pair of hydroxyl groups at the carbonyl carbon, allowing one to condense with chromic acid to enable over-oxidation to a carboxylic acid Example intermediate: C([*:1])C(O)O

name: Jones Oxidation
text: Hidden event (hydroxyalkyl chromate ester), seen in Jones Oxidation. Trigger: Condensation of a gem-diol (aldehyde hydrate) with an electrophilic chromium(VI) species under acidic conditions Role: Undergoes elimination of the remaining alpha-hydrogen with reduction of the chromium center to yield the carboxylic acid product Example intermediate: C([*:1])(O)O[Cr]([O-])(=O)(O)O

name: Julia-Kociensky Olefination
text: Hidden event (spirocyclic Smiles intermediate), seen in Julia-Kociensky Olefination. Trigger: Intramolecular nucleophilic attack of a beta-alkoxide onto an electron-deficient heteroaryl ring attached to an adjacent sulfone Role: Facilitates the Smiles rearrangement by opening with cleavage of the heteroaryl C-S bond to transfer the heteroaryl moiety from sulfur to oxygen Example intermediate: C1=CC=C2C(=C1)[N-]C3(S2)[S](=O)(c(C(O3)([*:3]))([*:1])[*:2])=O

name: Julia-Kociensky Olefination
text: Hidden event (beta-heteroaryloxy sulfinate), seen in Julia-Kociensky Olefination. Trigger: Collapse and C-S bond cleavage of the spirocyclic Smiles intermediate with rearomatization of the heteroaromatic ring Role: Undergoes spontaneous fragmentation with extrusion of sulfur dioxide and a heteroaryloxide leaving group to forge the alkene double bond Example intermediate: c1ccc2c(c1)n=c(s2)OC([*:3])C([*:1])([*:2])[S](=O)[O-]

name: Julia-Kociensky Olefination
text: Hidden event (beta-alkoxysulfone intermediate), seen in Julia-Kociensky Olefination. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of an alpha-sulfonyl carbanion to a carbonyl electrophile (aldehyde or ketone) Role: Provides the nucleophilic alkoxide oxygen correctly positioned to undergo intramolecular attack on the heteroaromatic ring Example intermediate: C([*:3])([O-])C([*:1])([*:2])S(=O)(=O)c1sc2ccccc2n1

name: Keck Asymmetric Allylation
text: Hidden event (beta-stannyl carbocation), seen in Keck Asymmetric Allylation. Trigger: Electrophilic addition of a Lewis acid-activated carbonyl or imine to an allylstannane, generating a carbocation adjacent to the C-Sn bond. Role: Stabilized by the beta-silicon/tin hyperconjugative effect, it rapidly undergoes C-Sn bond fragmentation (destannylation) to form the new carbon-carbon double bond. Example intermediate: C([*:3])(O)C([*:1])[C+]([*:2])C[Sn](CCCC)(CCCC)CCCC

name: Keck Asymmetric Allylation
text: Hidden event (Lewis acid-carbonyl adduct), seen in Keck Asymmetric Allylation. Trigger: Coordination of a carbonyl oxygen lone pair to a Lewis acidic metal center (such as a chiral titanium complex). Role: Lowers the energy of the carbonyl pi* orbital, drastically increasing electrophilicity to enable attack by weak nucleophiles such as allylstannanes. Example intermediate: O([Ti])=C([*:3])

name: Keck Asymmetric Allylation
text: Hidden event (stannyl ether), seen in Keck Asymmetric Allylation. Trigger: Transfer of the trialkyltin group to the newly formed alkoxide oxygen following C-C bond formation and destannylation. Role: Serves as a stable organometallic resting state of the product until protic workup hydrolyzes the O-Sn bond to liberate the homoallylic alcohol. Example intermediate: C([*:3])(O[Sn](CCCC)(CCCC)CCCC)C([*:1])C([*:2])=C

name: Knoevenagel Condensation
text: Hidden event (iminium ion), seen in Knoevenagel Condensation. Trigger: Condensation of a carbonyl group (aldehyde or ketone) with a secondary amine catalyst Role: Serves as an activated, highly electrophilic intermediate that accelerates addition by weakly nucleophilic active methylene compounds Example intermediate: C(=[N+]1CCCCC1)([*:3])[*:4]

name: Knoevenagel Condensation
text: Hidden event (beta-amino adduct), seen in Knoevenagel Condensation. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a stabilized carbanion or enolate to an iminium ion Role: Forms the key carbon-carbon bond while harboring an amine group primed for subsequent elimination to deliver the alkene product and regenerate the amine catalyst Example intermediate: C(C(N1CCCCC1)([*:3])[*:4])([*:1])[*:2]

name: Knorr Pyrrole Synthesis
text: Hidden event (3-hydroxydihydropyrrole), seen in Knorr Pyrrole Synthesis. Trigger: Intramolecular nucleophilic attack of an enamine carbon onto a tethered carbonyl group under acidic conditions Role: Closes the five-membered ring containing a hydroxyl leaving group primed for dehydration toward the aromatic product Example intermediate: C1(O)([*:1])C([*:2])NC([*:3])=C1(C(=O)O[*:4])

name: Knorr Pyrrole Synthesis
text: Hidden event (beta-enamino ester), seen in Knorr Pyrrole Synthesis. Trigger: Intermolecular condensation of a primary alpha-amino ketone with a 1,3-dicarbonyl compound under acidic conditions Role: Acts as an ambident nucleophile whose nucleophilic enamine beta-carbon attacks the remaining carbonyl group to achieve cyclization Example intermediate: C(C(O[*:4])=O)=C([*:3])NC([*:2])C(=O)[*:1]

name: Knorr Pyrrole Synthesis
text: Hidden event (2H-pyrrolium cation), seen in Knorr Pyrrole Synthesis. Trigger: Acid-catalyzed elimination of water from a 3-hydroxydihydropyrrole precursor Role: Undergoes deprotonation at the ring sp3 carbon to establish full pyrrole aromaticity Example intermediate: c1(c(C(=O)O[*:4])c([*:3])[nH+]C1[*:2])[*:1]

name: Knorr Quinoline Synthesis
text: Hidden event (cyclic carbinol intermediate), seen in Knorr Quinoline Synthesis. Trigger: A beta-ketoanilide (or aryl-tethered 1,3-dicarbonyl compound) under strongly acidic conditions, where intramolecular electrophilic aromatic attack of the aryl ring onto the activated carbonyl forms a six-membered cyclic alcohol. Role: Undergoes acid-catalyzed dehydration via protonation of the hydroxyl group and elimination of water, forging the C=C double bond and driving aromatization toward the quinolone system. Example intermediate: C1([*:1])=C2C(=C([*:4])C([*:3])=C1([*:2]))[NH+]=C(C([*:5])C2([*:6])O)O

name: Kochi Reaction
text: Hidden event (alkyl radical), seen in Kochi Reaction. Trigger: Homolytic cleavage of an acyl hypohalite or single-electron decarboxylation of a carboxylic acid derivative under thermal, photochemical, or redox conditions Role: Captures a halogen atom via ligand-transfer or atom-transfer to forge the carbon-halogen bond of the alkyl halide product Example intermediate: [*:1][C]

name: Kochi Reaction
text: Hidden event (acyl hypochlorite), seen in Kochi Reaction. Trigger: Reaction of a carboxylic acid or high-valent metal carboxylate with a chloride source under oxidative conditions Role: Undergoes homolysis of the weak oxygen-chlorine bond upon heating or irradiation to trigger radical decarboxylation Example intermediate: C(C[*:1])(=O)O(Cl)

name: Kochi Reaction
text: Hidden event (lead(IV) carboxylate), seen in Kochi Reaction. Trigger: Ligand exchange between a carboxylic acid and lead(IV) tetraacetate with displacement of an acetate ligand Role: Acts as an activated high-valent carboxylate intermediate poised for nucleophilic displacement by halide or single-electron transfer Example intermediate: C(C[*:1])(=O)O[Pb](OC(=O)C)(OC(=O)C)OC(=O)C

name: Kornblum Oxidation
text: Hidden event (alkoxysulfonium ion), seen in Kornblum Oxidation. Trigger: Nucleophilic substitution on an alkyl halide or sulfonate by the oxygen atom of a sulfoxide Role: Forms an activated covalent intermediate that activates the alkoxy moiety and acidifies the sulfur-bound alkyl protons for subsequent base deprotonation Example intermediate: C([*:1])O[S+](C)C

name: Kornblum Oxidation
text: Hidden event (sulfur ylide), seen in Kornblum Oxidation. Trigger: Deprotonation of an S-alkyl group of an alkoxysulfonium ion by a base Role: Serves as an internal base to abstract the alkoxy alpha-proton via a cyclic five-membered transition state, expelling a dialkyl sulfide to form the carbonyl product Example intermediate: C([*:1])O[S+](C)[CH2-]

name: Krapcho Decarboxylation
text: Hidden event (carboxylate anion), seen in Krapcho Decarboxylation. Trigger: An ester heated with a nucleophilic halide salt in a polar aprotic solvent, inducing SN2 cleavage of the ester alkyl group. Role: Undergoes thermal decarboxylation via heterolytic C-C bond cleavage to release carbon dioxide. Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])([*:3])C(=O)[O-]

name: Krapcho Decarboxylation
text: Hidden event (stabilized carbanion), seen in Krapcho Decarboxylation. Trigger: Extrusion of carbon dioxide from an alpha-electron-withdrawn carboxylate anion at elevated temperatures. Role: Acts as a strong base to abstract a proton from the reaction medium, delivering the neutral decarboxylated product. Example intermediate: [C-]([*:1])([*:2])([*:3])

name: Kucherov Reaction
text: Hidden event (vinyl cation), seen in Kucherov Reaction. Trigger: An alkyne exposed to a strong Brønsted acid or electrophilic activator Role: Acts as an electrophile that is captured by a nucleophile such as water to forge a carbon-heteroatom bond Example intermediate: [*:1][C+]=C

name: Kucherov Reaction
text: Hidden event (enol), seen in Kucherov Reaction. Trigger: Addition of water to an activated alkyne or vinyl cation followed by loss of a proton Role: Undergoes keto-enol tautomerization via carbon protonation and oxygen deprotonation to afford the thermodynamically favored carbonyl product Example intermediate: [*:1]C(O)=C

name: Kumada-Corriu Coupling
text: Hidden event (organopalladium(II) halide), seen in Kumada-Corriu Coupling. Trigger: Oxidative addition of an organic halide (typically an aryl, alkenyl, or alkyl halide) to a low-valent palladium(0) catalyst. Role: Serves as an electrophilic metal intermediate that undergoes transmetalation with an organometallic nucleophile to introduce the second carbon ligand. Example intermediate: [Pd]([*:1])Br

name: Kumada-Corriu Coupling
text: Hidden event (diorganopalladium(II) complex), seen in Kumada-Corriu Coupling. Trigger: Transmetalation between an organopalladium(II) halide and an organomagnesium reagent (Grignard reagent), displacing the halide ligand. Role: Brings the two organic coupling partners into proximity to undergo reductive elimination, forming the cross-coupled carbon-carbon bond and regenerating the palladium(0) catalyst. Example intermediate: [Pd]([*:1])[*:2]

name: Leimgruber-Batcho Indole Synthesis
text: Hidden event (indoleninium ion), seen in Leimgruber-Batcho Indole Synthesis. Trigger: Intramolecular nucleophilic attack of an ortho-arylamine onto an adjacent iminium moiety followed by expulsion of an amine leaving group Role: Undergoes deprotonation at C3 to rearomatize the pyrrole ring, furnishing the stable indole core Example intermediate: c1ccc2c(c1)C([*:2])C([*:3])=[NH+]2

name: Leimgruber-Batcho Indole Synthesis
text: Hidden event (iminium ion), seen in Leimgruber-Batcho Indole Synthesis. Trigger: Protonation of an electron-rich enamine at the beta-carbon under acidic or protic conditions Role: Acts as an activated electrophile that undergoes intramolecular attack by the pendant arylamine to initiate cyclization Example intermediate: Nc1ccccc1C([*:2])C([*:3])=[N+]([*:1])[*:1]

name: Lemieux-Johnson Oxidation
text: Hidden event (cyclic osmate ester), seen in Lemieux-Johnson Oxidation. Trigger: Concerted [3+2] cycloaddition of an alkene with osmium tetroxide (OsO4) Role: Serves as the key five-membered metallacycle intermediate that subsequently undergoes hydrolysis to deliver a syn-1,2-diol while reducing the osmium catalyst from Os(VIII) to Os(VI) Example intermediate: C1([*:1])([*:2])O[Os](=O)(=O)OC1([*:3])[*:4]

name: Lemieux-Johnson Oxidation
text: Hidden event (cyclic periodate ester), seen in Lemieux-Johnson Oxidation. Trigger: Condensation/addition of a vicinal diol onto periodate (IO4-) Role: Undergoes concerted retro-[3+2] cycloreversion/fragmentation to oxidatively cleave the central C-C bond, releasing two carbonyl fragments and reducing periodate to iodate Example intermediate: C1([*:1])([*:2])O[I](=O)(=O)(O)OC1([*:3])[*:4]

name: Ley-Griffith Oxidation
text: Hidden event (alkyl perruthenate ester), seen in Ley-Griffith Oxidation. Trigger: Addition of an alcohol hydroxyl group across a high-valent metal-oxo bond (e.g., perruthenate, chromate, permanganate) or ligand exchange with the metal center Role: Undergoes alpha-hydrogen abstraction / syn-elimination to forge the carbonyl C=O bond while reducing the metal center by two electrons Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])O[Ru](=O)(=O)(O)[O-]

name: Ley-Griffith Oxidation
text: Hidden event (reduced oxometal species), seen in Ley-Griffith Oxidation. Trigger: Two-electron reduction of a high-valent oxometal catalyst following hydride transfer / elimination from a coordinated alkoxide Role: Undergoes re-oxidation by a sacrificial terminal oxidant (such as an amine N-oxide) to regenerate the active oxometal catalyst and sustain catalytic turnover Example intermediate: O=[Ru](O)(O)[O-]

name: Lobry-de Bruyn-van Ekenstein Rearrangement
norm: lobry de bruyn van ekenstein rearrangement
text: Hidden event (enediol), seen in Lobry-de Bruyn-van Ekenstein Rearrangement. Trigger: Alpha-hydroxy carbonyl compound exposed to basic or acidic conditions Role: Undergoes tautomerization through proton transfer at the opposite oxygen and adjacent alkene carbon, yielding the isomeric alpha-hydroxy carbonyl compound Example intermediate: C(O)([*:2])=C(O)([*:1])

name: Lombardo Methylenation
text: Hidden event (gem-heterobimetallic complex), seen in Lombardo Methylenation. Trigger: Transmetalation of a gem-diorganozinc species with a high-valent transition metal halide (such as TiCl4) in an aprotic solvent. Role: Acts as an active, weakly basic alkylidene transfer agent that nucleophilically attacks carbonyls without triggering enolization. Example intermediate: Br[Zn]C[Ti](Cl)(Cl)Cl

name: Lombardo Methylenation
text: Hidden event (beta-metalloalkoxide adduct), seen in Lombardo Methylenation. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a gem-heterobimetallic alkylidene equivalent across the C=O bond of an aldehyde or ketone. Role: Undergoes fragmentation driven by the formation of strong metal-oxygen bonds to eliminate metal-oxo/halide species and forge the new alkene. Example intermediate: C(O[Ti](Cl)(Cl)Cl)([*:1])([*:2])C[Zn]Br

name: Lombardo Methylenation
text: Hidden event (gem-diorganozinc reagent), seen in Lombardo Methylenation. Trigger: Double oxidative addition of activated metallic zinc into both carbon-halogen bonds of a gem-dihaloalkane. Role: Serves as a dimetallated building block that undergoes transmetalation with transition metal halides to access heterobimetallic reagents. Example intermediate: Br[Zn]C[Zn]Br

name: Luche Reduction
text: Hidden event (Lewis acid-carbonyl adduct), seen in Luche Reduction. Trigger: Carbonyl compound (e.g., an enone or ketone) exposed to a hard, oxophilic Lewis acid (e.g., CeCl3 or other lanthanide salts) in polar or coordinating solvent. Role: Increases the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon and directs selective 1,2-hydride addition over 1,4-conjugate addition. Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])=C([*:3])C(=[O+][Ce-](Cl)(Cl)Cl)([*:4])

name: Luche Reduction
text: Hidden event (metal alkoxide intermediate), seen in Luche Reduction. Trigger: Nucleophilic hydride addition to a Lewis-acid-coordinated carbonyl group. Role: Acts as the transient adduct that undergoes protolysis by the protic solvent (MeOH) to afford the allylic alcohol and regenerate the Lewis acid catalyst. Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])=C([*:3])C(O[Ce-](Cl)(Cl)Cl)([*:4])

name: Madelung Indole Synthesis
text: Hidden event (cyclic tetrahedral intermediate), seen in Madelung Indole Synthesis. Trigger: Intramolecular nucleophilic addition of an ortho-benzylic carbanion to an adjacent carboxamide or acylamino carbonyl group under strongly basic conditions Role: Forms the five-membered heterocyclic ring and subsequently undergoes elimination of the oxygen functionality to establish the indole core Example intermediate: C1([*:6])([O-])[N-]c2ccccc2C1([*:5])

name: Madelung Indole Synthesis
text: Hidden event (indoleninium ion), seen in Madelung Indole Synthesis. Trigger: Nitrogen lone-pair-assisted elimination of a leaving group (water or hydroxide) from the 2-position of a 2-hydroxyindoline or cyclic hemiaminal Role: Undergoes rapid deprotonation at the adjacent C3 position to drive rearomatization to the stable 1H-indole product Example intermediate: C1([*:6])=[NH+]c2ccccc2C1([*:5])

name: Maitland-Japp Reaction
text: Hidden event (beta-hydroxy enone), seen in Maitland-Japp Reaction. Trigger: Acid-catalyzed aldol addition of the remaining enolizable alpha-position of an alpha,beta-unsaturated ketone to an aldehyde Role: Acts as the bifunctional acyclic precursor that positions a pendant nucleophilic hydroxyl group for intramolecular oxa-Michael addition across the conjugated enone Example intermediate: C([*:3])=C([*:1])C(=O)C([*:2])C(O)([*:4])

name: Maitland-Japp Reaction
text: Hidden event (alpha,beta-unsaturated ketone), seen in Maitland-Japp Reaction. Trigger: Acid-catalyzed aldol condensation between a ketone bearing an alpha-methylene group and an aldehyde, accompanied by dehydration Role: Serves as an activated electrophilic scaffold that undergoes a second aldol addition at its remaining alpha-position and provides the Michael acceptor for subsequent ring closure Example intermediate: C([*:2])C(=O)C(=C([*:3]))([*:1])

name: Maitland-Japp Reaction
text: Hidden event (cyclic enol), seen in Maitland-Japp Reaction. Trigger: Intramolecular oxa-Michael addition of a tethered hydroxyl group to an activated enone, followed by deprotonation Role: Undergoes keto-enol tautomerization to furnish the thermodynamically favored tetrahydropyran-4-one product Example intermediate: C1([*:3])C([*:1])=C(O)C([*:2])C([*:4])O1

name: Mannich Reaction
text: Hidden event (enol), seen in Mannich Reaction. Trigger: A carbonyl compound possessing an alpha-hydrogen under acidic conditions, where protonation of the carbonyl oxygen is followed by deprotonation at the alpha-carbon. Role: Acts as a carbon nucleophile via its alpha-carbon, attacking an electrophilic species to forge a new carbon-carbon bond. Example intermediate: C([*:3])([*:2])=C(O)[*:1]

name: Markó-Lam Deoxygenation
text: Hidden event (metal ketyl radical), seen in Markó-Lam Deoxygenation. Trigger: Single-electron reduction of a carbonyl group (such as an ester or carboxyl derivative) by a low-valent metal reductant like SmI2 in the presence of coordinating Lewis-base ligands (e.g., HMPA). Role: Undergoes homolytic beta-scission of the adjacent C-O bond, expelling the carboxylate-samarium salt and releasing an alkyl radical. Example intermediate: C(O[C]([O][Sm](I)I)[*:4])([*:1])([*:2])([*:3])

name: Markó-Lam Deoxygenation
text: Hidden event (alkyl radical), seen in Markó-Lam Deoxygenation. Trigger: Homolytic C-O bond fragmentation (beta-scission) of an alkoxy-substituted ketyl radical intermediate. Role: Abstracts a hydrogen atom from a hydrogen donor (such as an added protic/hydride source or solvent) to deliver the deoxygenated alkane product. Example intermediate: [C]([*:1])([*:2])([*:3])

name: McMurry Reaction
text: Hidden event (titanium pinacolate), seen in McMurry Reaction. Trigger: Radical-radical C-C coupling of two ketyl radicals coordinated to a low-valent, oxophilic titanium template, yielding a five-membered 1,3,2-dioxatitanolane metallacycle Role: Undergoes deoxygenative elimination driven by the high thermodynamic stability of titanium-oxygen bonds (forming titanyl species), extruding the titanium oxide byproduct and yielding the alkene Example intermediate: C1([*:1])([*:2])O[Ti](Cl)(Cl)OC1([*:3])([*:4])

name: McMurry Reaction
text: Hidden event (metal-bound ketyl radical), seen in McMurry Reaction. Trigger: Single-electron reduction of a carbonyl group (aldehyde or ketone) by a low-valent transition metal reagent such as Ti(0) or Ti(II) Role: Acts as a persistent carbon-centered radical coordinated to the metal template that couples with another ketyl radical to forge the central C-C bond Example intermediate: [C](O[Ti](Cl)(Cl))([*:1])([*:2])

name: Meerwein-Ponndorf-Verley Reduction
text: Hidden event (lewis_acid_carbonyl_complex), seen in Meerwein-Ponndorf-Verley Reduction. Trigger: Coordination of a Lewis-basic carbonyl oxygen to a vacant coordination site on a Lewis-acidic metal alkoxide. Role: Lowers the LUMO of the carbonyl, activating it toward nucleophilic attack, and organizes the complex into a six-membered cyclic transition state for hydride delivery. Example intermediate: C(=[O+][Al-](OC(C)C)(OC(C)C)OC(C)C)([*:1])([*:2])

name: Meerwein-Ponndorf-Verley Reduction
text: Hidden event (metal_alkoxide), seen in Meerwein-Ponndorf-Verley Reduction. Trigger: Intramolecular beta-hydride transfer from an alkoxide ligand to the activated carbonyl carbon with concomitant extrusion of a ketone byproduct. Role: Acts as the catalyst-bound product adduct, which undergoes ligand exchange (alcoholysis) with an excess of secondary alcohol solvent to release the free alcohol product and regenerate the metal catalyst. Example intermediate: C(O[Al](OC(C)C)OC(C)C)([*:1])([*:2])

name: Meyer-Schuster Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (propargylic / allenyl carbocation), seen in Meyer-Schuster Rearrangement. Trigger: Loss of water (or another leaving group) from a propargylic position under acidic or Lewis acidic conditions. Role: Delocalizes charge between the propargylic and acetylenic termini, directing nucleophilic attack by water to the distal alkyne carbon to establish an allene framework. Example intermediate: [C+](C#C[*:1])([*:2])([*:3])

name: Meyer-Schuster Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (allenol), seen in Meyer-Schuster Rearrangement. Trigger: Addition of water to the distal carbon of a propargyl/allenyl carbocation, followed by deprotonation. Role: Acts as the key transient enol-like intermediate that undergoes acid-catalyzed keto-enol-type tautomerization to yield the final conjugated enone. Example intermediate: C(O)([*:1])=C=C([*:2])([*:3])

name: Michael Addition
text: Hidden event (enolate intermediate), seen in Michael Addition. Trigger: Conjugate (1,4-) addition of a nucleophile to an alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl compound under basic conditions Role: Accepts the electron density from nucleophilic attack, temporarily storing it on oxygen before undergoing C-protonation at the alpha-position to restore the carbonyl group Example intermediate: S([*:4])C([*:1])([*:2])C([*:3])=C([O-])[*:5]

name: Michaelis-Arbuzov Reaction
text: Hidden event (alkoxyphosphonium intermediate), seen in Michaelis-Arbuzov Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic attack of a trivalent phosphorus ester (such as a phosphite) on an sp3 carbon bearing a leaving group (such as an alkyl halide). Role: The positively charged phosphorus atom strongly activates the attached alkoxy carbons toward nucleophilic attack by the displaced halide counterion, promoting an SN2 dealkylation to yield a thermodynamically favorable phosphoryl (P=O) bond. Example intermediate: [P+](O[*:3])(O[*:3])(O[*:3])[CH]([*:1])([*:2]).[Br-]

name: Mitsunobu Reaction
text: Hidden event (alkoxyphosphonium intermediate), seen in Mitsunobu Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic attack of an alcohol oxygen onto an electrophilic phosphonium center, displacing a heteroatom leaving group. Role: Activates the alcohol hydroxyl group toward bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (SN2) by creating a triphenylphosphine oxide leaving group, enabling substitution with clean inversion of configuration. Example intermediate: [C@@H](O[P+](c1ccccc1)(c2ccccc2)c3ccccc3)([*:1])([*:2])

name: Mitsunobu Reaction
text: Hidden event (phosphonium zwitterion), seen in Mitsunobu Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a tertiary phosphine to an electron-deficient azo compound (such as a dialkyl azodicarboxylate). Role: Serves as a reactive basic adduct that deprotonates the pronucleophile and generates the electrophilic phosphonium intermediate necessary for alcohol activation. Example intermediate: c1ccccc1[P+](c2ccccc2)(c3ccccc3)N([N-]C(=O)OCC)C(=O)OCC

name: Morita-Baylis-Hillman Reaction
text: Hidden event (zwitterionic enolate), seen in Morita-Baylis-Hillman Reaction. Trigger: Conjugate addition of a nucleophilic Lewis base catalyst (such as a tertiary amine or phosphine) to an electron-deficient alkene Role: Acts as a carbon nucleophile at the alpha-position to attack an aldehyde or other carbonyl electrophile, forming a new carbon-carbon bond Example intermediate: C([*:4])(=CC([*:1])([*:2])[N+]12CCN(CC1)CC2)[O-]

name: Morita-Baylis-Hillman Reaction
text: Hidden event (betaine alkoxide intermediate), seen in Morita-Baylis-Hillman Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a catalyst-bound enolate onto a carbonyl electrophile Role: Undergoes proton transfer from the alpha position to the alkoxide oxygen, priming the system for beta-elimination of the catalyst Example intermediate: C([*:1])(C(C([*:2])([*:3])[N+]12CCN(CC1)CC2)C([*:5])[O-])=O

name: Mukaiyama Aldol Addition
text: Hidden event (silyloxonium ion), seen in Mukaiyama Aldol Addition. Trigger: Coordination or transfer of a silyl group (or strong Lewis acid) to a carbonyl oxygen under acidic or Lewis acidic conditions Role: Increases the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon, enabling attack by a relatively weak carbon nucleophile like a silyl enol ether Example intermediate: C(=[O+][Si]([*:4])([*:4])([*:4]))([*:5])([*:6])

name: Mukaiyama Aldol Addition
text: Hidden event (silyl ether), seen in Mukaiyama Aldol Addition. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a silyl enol ether to an activated carbonyl electrophile with concomitant transfer of the silyl group to the nascent alkoxide Role: Acts as the protected aldol addition adduct that undergoes subsequent desilylation/hydrolysis to reveal the beta-hydroxy carbonyl product Example intermediate: [*:1]C(=O)C([*:2])([*:3])C(O[Si]([*:4])([*:4])([*:4]))([*:5])([*:6])

name: Myers Asymmetric Alkylation
text: Hidden event (amide enolate), seen in Myers Asymmetric Alkylation. Trigger: An amide bearing an alpha-hydrogen and a directing hydroxy group treated with a strong non-nucleophilic base (such as LDA) Role: Acts as a carbon nucleophile, undergoing nucleophilic substitution (SN2) on an alkyl halide to form a new carbon-carbon bond with high stereocontrol Example intermediate: [*:1]/C=C(\[O-])/N(C)C(C)C([O-])c1ccccc1

name: Nazarov Cyclization Reaction
text: Hidden event (carbocation), seen in Nazarov Cyclization Reaction. Trigger: A divinyl ketone (1,4-dien-3-one) activated by a Brønsted or Lewis acid undergoes 4π electrocyclization. Role: Undergoes deprotonation (elimination of a proton) to form an enol intermediate that tautomerizes to the cyclopentenone product. Example intermediate: C1(=CC(C([CH+]1)C([*:1]))C([*:2]))O

name: Neber Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (2H-azirine), seen in Neber Rearrangement. Trigger: Deprotonation at the alpha-position of a ketoxime derivative bearing a leaving group on nitrogen (e.g., an oxime sulfonate) by base, followed by intramolecular nucleophilic attack of the alpha-carbanion onto the nitrogen atom with displacement of the leaving group. Role: Acts as an electrophilic, strained three-membered ring intermediate that undergoes nucleophilic attack by water or hydroxide across the C=N double bond. Example intermediate: [*:3]C2=NC([*:1])([*:2])2

name: Neber Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (aziridin-2-olate), seen in Neber Rearrangement. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of water or hydroxide to the electrophilic C=N double bond of a 2H-azirine, followed by proton transfer to form an oxyanion. Role: Drives endocyclic C-N bond cleavage via collapse of the oxyanion to form a carbonyl group, yielding the alpha-aminoketone framework. Example intermediate: C([*:3])2(C([*:1])([*:2])[NH]2)[O-]

name: Nef Reaction
text: Hidden event (tetrahedral intermediate), seen in Nef Reaction. Trigger: nucleophilic addition of water to an activated iminium-like carbon, such as a protonated nitronic acid, under aqueous acidic conditions Role: undergoes elimination of the nitrogen-containing leaving group driven by the formation of the carbon-oxygen double bond to yield the carbonyl product Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])([NH+](O)O)[OH]

name: Nef Reaction
text: Hidden event (iminium ion), seen in Nef Reaction. Trigger: protonation of the second oxygen of a nitronic acid (aci-nitro species) in strong aqueous acid Role: strongly activates the carbon-nitrogen double bond toward nucleophilic attack by weak nucleophiles like water Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])=[N+](O)O

name: Nef Reaction
text: Hidden event (nitronic acid), seen in Nef Reaction. Trigger: O-protonation of a nitronate anion or acid-catalyzed tautomerization of a nitroalkane Role: serves as the reactive imine-like tautomer of a nitro group that can be further activated toward nucleophilic addition Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])=[N+]([O-])O

name: Nenitzescu Indole Synthesis
text: Hidden event (carbinolamine), seen in Nenitzescu Indole Synthesis. Trigger: Intramolecular nucleophilic attack of an amino or enamino nitrogen onto a proximate carbonyl group (e.g., a quinone ketone) under mildly acidic conditions. Role: Acts as the cyclized tetrahedral intermediate that undergoes acid-catalyzed dehydration to drive indole ring construction. Example intermediate: C1=C(C=CC3(C1C(=C(C2=CC=CC=C2)N3([*:2]))C(=O)O([*:3]))O)O

name: Nenitzescu Indole Synthesis
text: Hidden event (indoleninium ion), seen in Nenitzescu Indole Synthesis. Trigger: Acid-promoted elimination of water from a cyclic carbinolamine (3-hydroxyindoline) intermediate. Role: Serves as a high-energy cyclic iminium species that rapidly loses a proton to establish aromaticity in the indole nucleus. Example intermediate: C1=C(C=CC3(C1C(=C(C2=CC=CC=C2)[N+]=3([*:2]))C(=O)O([*:3])))O

name: Nenitzescu Indole Synthesis
text: Hidden event (iminium ion), seen in Nenitzescu Indole Synthesis. Trigger: Conjugate (Michael-type) addition of an enamine carbon to an electron-deficient enone or quinone. Role: Undergoes tautomerization and deprotonation to re-establish the neutral enamine moiety required for downstream cyclization. Example intermediate: C1=C(C=CC(C1C(C(C2=CC=CC=C2)=[NH+]([*:2]))C(=O)O([*:3]))=O)O

name: Nierenstein reaction
text: Hidden event (tetrahedral_intermediate), seen in Nierenstein reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a carbon nucleophile (such as a diazoalkane) to an acyl halide carbonyl group Role: Re-forms the carbonyl C=O double bond, driving the displacement of dinitrogen by chloride to yield the alpha-chloroketone Example intermediate: C([O-])(Cl)(C[N+]#N)([*:1])

name: Norrish Reaction
text: Hidden event (acyl radical), seen in Norrish Reaction. Trigger: Carbonyl compound (ketone or aldehyde) under photochemical irradiation (hv) undergoing homolytic alpha-cleavage (Norrish Type I process). Role: Participates in hydrogen abstraction (disproportionation) with the partner radical, decarbonylates to release carbon monoxide, or recombines. Example intermediate: [CH3]C=O

name: Norrish Reaction
text: Hidden event (alkyl radical), seen in Norrish Reaction. Trigger: Aliphatic carbon alpha to a carbonyl group released through photochemical homolytic C-C bond cleavage. Role: Undergoes disproportionation via beta-hydrogen transfer to yield an alkene product, or terminates via radical coupling. Example intermediate: [CH2]C([*:1])

name: Oppenauer Oxidation
text: Hidden event (carbonyl-Lewis acid complex), seen in Oppenauer Oxidation. Trigger: Coordination of a carbonyl oxygen to the Lewis-acidic metal center of an aluminium alkoxide Role: Activates the carbonyl electrophile and organizes a cyclic six-membered transition state for intramolecular hydride transfer from the alkoxide alpha-carbon Example intermediate: C([*:3])([*:4])[O][Al-](OC(C)C)([O+]=C([*:1])([*:2]))OC(C)C

name: Oppenauer Oxidation
text: Hidden event (aluminium alkoxide), seen in Oppenauer Oxidation. Trigger: Ligand exchange of an alcohol substrate onto an aluminium trialkoxide (such as aluminium isopropoxide) Role: Serves as the activated hydride-donor substrate while retaining Lewis acidity to coordinate the oxidant carbonyl Example intermediate: C([*:3])([*:4])[O][Al](OC(C)C)OC(C)C

name: Oppenauer Oxidation
text: Hidden event (alcohol-Lewis acid adduct), seen in Oppenauer Oxidation. Trigger: Coordination of a neutral alcohol oxygen lone pair to a Lewis-acidic aluminium trialkoxide Role: Acidifies the hydroxyl proton to facilitate proton transfer to a coordinated alkoxide ligand, driving alcohol displacement Example intermediate: C([*:3])([*:4])[OH+][Al-](OC(C)C)(OC(C)C)OC(C)C

name: Paal-Knorr Furan Synthesis
text: Hidden event (oxocarbenium ion), seen in Paal-Knorr Furan Synthesis. Trigger: Acid-catalyzed elimination of water from a cyclic hemiacetal or 2-hydroxy-2,3-dihydrofuran intermediate. Role: Undergoes rapid deprotonation at the adjacent ring position to establish aromaticity and form the furan ring. Example intermediate: C=1C([*:1])[O+]=C([*:2])C1

name: Paal-Knorr Furan Synthesis
text: Hidden event (cyclic hemiacetal), seen in Paal-Knorr Furan Synthesis. Trigger: Intramolecular nucleophilic addition of a carbonyl oxygen onto a protonated carbonyl group within a 1,4-dicarbonyl compound under acidic conditions. Role: Acts as the cyclized five-membered ring intermediate that undergoes acid-promoted dehydration to drive aromatization. Example intermediate: C1C([*:1])([OH])[O]C([*:2])=C1

name: Parikh-Doering Oxidation
text: Hidden event (activated sulfoxide adduct), seen in Parikh-Doering Oxidation. Trigger: Nucleophilic attack of a sulfoxide oxygen onto an electrophilic activating agent such as sulfur trioxide or an acyl/oxalyl chloride Role: Converts the sulfoxide into an electrophilic sulfur center susceptible to nucleophilic attack by an alcohol Example intermediate: C[S+]([*:1])O[S](=O)(=O)[O-]

name: Parikh-Doering Oxidation
text: Hidden event (alkoxysulfonium ylide), seen in Parikh-Doering Oxidation. Trigger: Deprotonation of an alpha-proton adjacent to the positively polarized sulfur atom of an alkoxysulfonium species by a tertiary amine base Role: Undergoes an intramolecular five-membered cyclic elimination to forge the carbonyl C=O bond while releasing a dialkyl sulfide leaving group Example intermediate: [S]([*:1])(=C)O(C([*:2])([*:3]))

name: Parikh-Doering Oxidation
text: Hidden event (hypervalent sulfurane intermediate), seen in Parikh-Doering Oxidation. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of an alcohol oxygen to an activated sulfonium center prior to leaving group expulsion Role: Facilitates the addition-elimination sequence at sulfur, collapsing with loss of the sulfate leaving group Example intermediate: C([S]([*:1])(O([S](=O)(=O)[O-]))O(C([*:2])([*:3])))

name: Passerini Reaction
text: Hidden event (nitrilium ion), seen in Passerini Reaction.
