Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of an isocyanide carbon to an activated (e.g., protonated) carbonyl group Role: Acts as a potent carbon electrophile that rapidly traps a carboxylic acid to forge the three-component adduct Example intermediate: OC([*:1])([*:2])C(#[N+][*:3])

name: Passerini Reaction
text: Hidden event (cyclic tetrahedral intermediate), seen in Passerini Reaction. Trigger: Intramolecular nucleophilic attack of a tethered hydroxyl group onto an imidoyl carboxylate carbonyl Role: Facilitates a Mumm-type rearrangement by collapsing to break the imidoyl C-O bond, irreversibly transferring the acyl group and forming the amide carbonyl Example intermediate: [OH]C2([*:4])OC(=[N][*:3])C([*:1])([*:2])O2

name: Passerini Reaction
text: Hidden event (imidoyl carboxylate), seen in Passerini Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a carboxylic acid (or carboxylate) to a nitrilium intermediate Role: Assembles the complete three-component adduct and positions the acyl group for intramolecular transfer to the adjacent hydroxyl group Example intermediate: [OH+]=C([*:4])OC(=[N][*:3])C([*:1])([*:2])O

name: Paterno-Buchi Reaction
text: Hidden event (1,4-diradical), seen in Paterno-Buchi Reaction. Trigger: Photochemical irradiation of a carbonyl compound in the presence of an alkene, leading to addition of the excited carbonyl oxygen to the alkene pi bond Role: Undergoes spin inversion (if triplet) and radical-radical coupling to form the second ring bond, closing the oxetane ring and dictating regio- and stereochemical outcomes Example intermediate: [C]([*:1])([*:2])C([*:3])([*:4])O[C]([*:5])([*:6])

name: Payne Epoxidation
text: Hidden event (peroxycarboximidic acid), seen in Payne Epoxidation. Trigger: Addition of hydrogen peroxide to a nitrile under mildly basic conditions, followed by proton transfer Role: Acts as an electrophilic oxygen-transfer agent that epoxidizes the alkene while being reduced to a primary carboxamide Example intermediate: OOC(=N)[*:1]

name: Payne Epoxidation
text: Hidden event (peroxycarboximidate anion), seen in Payne Epoxidation. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of hydroperoxide anion to the electrophilic carbon of a nitrile Role: Undergoes rapid protonation to yield the neutral peroxycarboximidic acid epoxidizing agent Example intermediate: [N-]=C(OO)[*:1]

name: Payne Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (oxiranium ion), seen in Payne Rearrangement. Trigger: Protonation of an epoxy alcohol (an oxirane ring bearing an adjacent hydroxyl group) under acidic conditions Role: Activates the strained three-membered ring toward intramolecular nucleophilic attack by the neighboring hydroxyl oxygen, initiating the 1,2-shift / epoxide migration Example intermediate: C12C(CCCC1([*:1])O)[OH+]2

name: Payne Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (oxiranium ion), seen in Payne Rearrangement. Trigger: Intramolecular nucleophilic attack of an adjacent hydroxyl group onto an activated protonated epoxide via a 1,2-shift rearrangement Role: Undergoes deprotonation by solvent or conjugate base to afford the neutral, isomeric epoxy alcohol product Example intermediate: C12C(CCCC1([*:1])[OH+]2)O

name: Pechmann Condensation
text: Hidden event (arenium ion), seen in Pechmann Condensation. Trigger: An aromatic ring undergoing intramolecular attack by an activated, protonated carbonyl electrophile under acidic conditions. Role: Deprotonates at the newly substituted ring position to restore aromaticity, driving electrophilic aromatic substitution to completion. Example intermediate: OC(C([*:2])([*:3])([*:4]))1CC(=[O])O[C+]2C([*:1])=CC=CC21

name: Pechmann Condensation
text: Hidden event (enol), seen in Pechmann Condensation. Trigger: A carbonyl compound (such as a lactone) bearing an acidic alpha-hydrogen under acidic conditions undergoing enolization. Role: Serves as a transient tautomer that facilitates elimination of the beta-hydroxy group to forge a conjugated alpha,beta-unsaturated lactone. Example intermediate: OC(C([*:2])([*:3])([*:4]))1C=C(O)Oc2c([*:1])cccc21

name: Petasis-Ferrier Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (oxocarbenium ion), seen in Petasis-Ferrier Rearrangement. Trigger: Lewis acid-assisted heterolytic cleavage of a cyclic acetal or enol acetal C-O bond Role: Acts as an electrophile that undergoes intramolecular nucleophilic attack by the tethered enol or enolate to construct the rearranged ring system Example intermediate: C=[O+]CCC([OH])=C([*:1])([*:2])

name: Petasis-Ferrier Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (Lewis acid-base adduct), seen in Petasis-Ferrier Rearrangement. Trigger: Coordination of an ether or acetal oxygen atom to a Lewis acid (e.g., an organoaluminum halide) Role: Polarizes and weakens the adjacent carbon-oxygen bond, promoting ring opening to generate an oxocarbenium intermediate Example intermediate: C1[O+]([Al]([*:1])([*:2]))C(CCO1)=C(C)C

name: Petrenko-Kritschenko Piperidone Synthesis
text: Hidden event (iminium ion), seen in Petrenko-Kritschenko Piperidone Synthesis. Trigger: Condensation of an aldehyde with ammonia or an amine under acidic conditions, followed by dehydration of the carbinolamine intermediate. Role: Acts as the key electrophile for nucleophilic addition by the enol tautomer of an active methylene (1,3-dicarbonyl) compound to form a carbon-carbon bond. Example intermediate: [NH2+]=CC([*:2])

name: Petrenko-Kritschenko Piperidone Synthesis
text: Hidden event (hemiaminal), seen in Petrenko-Kritschenko Piperidone Synthesis. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of ammonia or an amine to an aldehyde or ketone carbonyl group under neutral or acidic conditions. Role: Acts as the initial covalent adduct that undergoes protonation and elimination of water to form a reactive imine or iminium ion. Example intermediate: NC(O)C([*:2])

name: Pfitzner-Moffatt oxidation
text: Hidden event (alkoxysulfonium ylide), seen in Pfitzner-Moffatt oxidation. Trigger: Deprotonation of an alpha-methyl (or methylene) carbon of an alkoxysulfonium intermediate by a base. Role: Undergoes an intramolecular five-membered cyclic elimination (proton abstraction from the alkoxy carbon) to yield the carbonyl product and dimethyl sulfide. Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])[O][S](=C)C

name: Pfitzner-Moffatt oxidation
text: Hidden event (isourea-sulfonium adduct), seen in Pfitzner-Moffatt oxidation. Trigger: Nucleophilic attack of a sulfoxide oxygen onto a carbodiimide in the presence of a mild acid catalyst. Role: Serves as an activated electrophilic sulfur intermediate that is attacked by an alcohol, setting up urea as an excellent leaving group. Example intermediate: N([*:6])=C(N([*:6]))O[S+](C)C

name: Pfitzner-Moffatt oxidation
text: Hidden event (sulfurane intermediate), seen in Pfitzner-Moffatt oxidation. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of an alcohol oxygen to an activated sulfonium center bearing a leaving group. Role: Acts as a transient hypervalent (10-S-4) sulfur species that rapidly collapses with expulsion of the neutral urea leaving group to forge the alkoxysulfonium species. Example intermediate: [NH]([*:6])C(=[NH+]([*:6]))OS(C)(C)OC([*:1])([*:2])

name: Piancatelli Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (hydroxypentadienyl cation), seen in Piancatelli Rearrangement. Trigger: Acid-promoted ring opening and C-O bond cleavage of a 5-hydroxy-2-alkylidenedihydrofuran intermediate Role: Undergoes a conrotatory 4pi electrocyclic ring closure (Nazarov-type cyclization) to forge the cyclopentenone carbon skeleton Example intermediate: C(=[OH+])C=CC([OH])=C[*:1]

name: Piancatelli Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (furfuryl carbocation), seen in Piancatelli Rearrangement. Trigger: Acid-catalyzed ionization and departure of a leaving group from the exocyclic position of a 2-furyl carbinol Role: Acts as an electrophile that undergoes conjugate addition of water at the C5 position of the furan ring Example intermediate: [CH+](c1occc1)[*:1]

name: Piancatelli Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (dihydrofuran oxonium ion), seen in Piancatelli Rearrangement. Trigger: Nucleophilic attack of water at the C5 position of an activated furfuryl carbocation Role: Undergoes proton transfer to the furan ring oxygen, setting up ring-opening elimination Example intermediate: C1=CC([OH2+])OC1=C[*:1]

name: Pictet-Spengler Reaction
text: Hidden event (iminium ion), seen in Pictet-Spengler Reaction. Trigger: Condensation of an aldehyde or ketone with an amine under acidic or dehydrating conditions. Role: Serves as a strong carbon electrophile that undergoes intramolecular attack by a tethered electron-rich aromatic ring to forge a new carbon-carbon bond. Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])=[NH+]C(CC1=CNC2=C1C=CC=C2)

name: Pictet-Spengler Reaction
text: Hidden event (arenium ion), seen in Pictet-Spengler Reaction. Trigger: Electrophilic attack onto an electron-rich aromatic ring by a carbon electrophile, temporarily disrupting aromaticity. Role: Undergoes proton elimination to re-establish the stable aromatic ring system and furnish the cyclized product. Example intermediate: C1([*:1])([*:2])NCCC2C1=[NH+]C3=C2C=CC=C3

name: Pinacol Coupling
text: Hidden event (magnesium pinacolate), seen in Pinacol Coupling. Trigger: Two carbonyl groups (aldehydes or ketones) undergoing single-electron reduction by an electropositive metal (such as Mg) followed by radical-radical coupling of the resulting ketyl species Role: Undergoes hydrolysis and proton transfer upon aqueous or acidic workup, cleaving the magnesium-oxygen bonds to release the vicinal 1,2-diol (pinacol) product Example intermediate: [CH]([*:1])O[Mg]O[CH]C([*:1])

name: Pinacol Coupling
text: Hidden event (ketyl radical), seen in Pinacol Coupling. Trigger: Carbonyl group (aldehyde or ketone) exposed to a single-electron reducing metal (such as Mg, Sm, or Na) undergoing single-electron transfer (SET) Role: Undergoes radical-radical dimerization with a second ketyl radical to form the central carbon-carbon bond of the pinacol framework Example intermediate: [CH.]([*:1])[O-]

name: Pinacol Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (beta-hydroxy carbocation), seen in Pinacol Rearrangement. Trigger: Acid-catalyzed ionization of a vicinal diol via protonation of a hydroxyl group followed by departure of water as a leaving group. Role: Serves as the electrophilic sink that drives a 1,2-shift (hydride, alkyl, or aryl migration) assisted by the lone pair of the adjacent hydroxyl oxygen to form a carbonyl group. Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])(O)[C+]([*:3])([*:4])

name: Pinner Reaction
text: Hidden event (tetrahedral intermediate), seen in Pinner Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of an amine or ammonia to an imidate (imino ether) or its protonated form Role: Undergoes proton transfer to activate the alkoxy substituent as a leaving group, followed by elimination of alcohol to generate an amidinium species Example intermediate: C([*:1])(N)([NH2])OCC

name: Pinnick-Lindgren Oxidation
text: Hidden event (chlorite hemiacetal), seen in Pinnick-Lindgren Oxidation. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of chlorite (or chlorous acid) to an aldehyde carbonyl under weakly acidic, buffered conditions Role: Undergoes cyclic fragmentation via C–H bond cleavage to eliminate hypochlorous acid (HOCl) and yield the carboxylic acid Example intermediate: C([*:1])C(O)O(Cl=O)

name: Polonovski-Potier Reaction
text: Hidden event (N-acyloxyammonium ion), seen in Polonovski-Potier Reaction. Trigger: Treatment of a tertiary amine N-oxide with an activating acylating agent such as an anhydride or acid chloride Role: Serves as an activated intermediate where the acyloxy group serves as a leaving group, enabling subsequent alpha-deprotonation and elimination to form an iminium ion Example intermediate: C1CCC[N+]([O]C(=O)C(F)(F)F)(C([*:1])([*:2])([*:3]))C1

name: Polonovski-Potier Reaction
text: Hidden event (tetrahedral intermediate), seen in Polonovski-Potier Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a tertiary amine N-oxide oxygen to an electrophilic anhydride carbonyl group Role: Collapses via expulsion of a carboxylate leaving group to complete acyl transfer, furnishing the O-acylated ammonium species Example intermediate: C1CCC[N+]([O]C([O-])(C(F)(F)F)OC(=O)C(F)(F)F)(C([*:1])([*:2])([*:3]))C1

name: Pomeranz-Fritsch Isoquinoline Synthesis
text: Hidden event (oxocarbenium ion), seen in Pomeranz-Fritsch Isoquinoline Synthesis. Trigger: Acid-catalyzed elimination of an alkoxy leaving group from an acetal or ketal. Role: Acts as a potent electrophilic intermediate that undergoes deprotonation at the adjacent carbon to generate an enol ether. Example intermediate: C(c1ccccc1)([*:1])=NC(c1ccccc1)C(=[O+]CC)

name: Pomeranz-Fritsch Isoquinoline Synthesis
text: Hidden event (enol ether), seen in Pomeranz-Fritsch Isoquinoline Synthesis. Trigger: Deprotonation of the carbon alpha to an oxocarbenium ion under acidic conditions. Role: Participates in intramolecular ring closure via electrophilic aromatic substitution, consuming the transient carbon-carbon double bond. Example intermediate: C(c1ccccc1)([*:1])=NC(c1ccccc1)=C([O]CC)

name: Pomeranz-Fritsch Isoquinoline Synthesis
text: Hidden event (cyclized adduct), seen in Pomeranz-Fritsch Isoquinoline Synthesis. Trigger: Intramolecular cyclization of an enol ether onto a pendant aromatic ring. Role: Undergoes elimination of an alcohol leaving group (rearomatization) to yield the fully aromatic isoquinoline system. Example intermediate: C(=C1C2C=CC=C1)([*:1])N=C(c1ccccc1)C2([O]CC)

name: Prins Reaction
text: Hidden event (carbocation), seen in Prins Reaction. Trigger: Electrophilic addition of a protonated (or Lewis acid-activated) carbonyl compound onto an alkene double bond under acidic conditions Role: Acts as a potent electrophile that captures a nucleophile (such as water) to form the addition product, or undergoes elimination/cyclization Example intermediate: [C+]([*:4])([*:5])C([*:3])(C(O)([*:1])([*:2]))

name: Pummerer Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (thionium ion), seen in Pummerer Rearrangement. Trigger: Deprotonation at the alpha-position of an activated sulfonium species bearing a leaving group on sulfur, coupled with elimination of that leaving group. Role: Acts as a potent carbon electrophile that undergoes nucleophilic attack at the alpha-carbon, yielding an alpha-functionalized sulfide. Example intermediate: [S+](=C[*:1])([*:2])

name: Pummerer Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (acyloxysulfonium ion), seen in Pummerer Rearrangement. Trigger: Acylation of a sulfoxide oxygen by an electrophilic acylating agent (e.g., an anhydride or acyl chloride) upon expulsion of the leaving group. Role: Greatly increases the acidity of adjacent alpha C-H protons and activates the S-O bond for cleavage, priming the molecule for elimination to a thionium ion. Example intermediate: [S+](OC(=[O])(C))(C[*:1])([*:2])

name: Pummerer Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (tetrahedral intermediate), seen in Pummerer Rearrangement. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a sulfoxide oxygen to the carbonyl carbon of an acylating agent. Role: Collapses via reformation of the carbonyl C=O bond and expulsion of carboxylate to form an activated sulfonium intermediate. Example intermediate: [S+](OC([O-])(C)OC(=O)C)(C[*:1])([*:2])

name: Seyferth-Gilbert Homologation
text: Hidden event (alkylidene carbene), seen in Seyferth-Gilbert Homologation. Trigger: Extrusion of dinitrogen from a diazoalkene or alpha-elimination of a haloalkene under basic conditions Role: Undergoes a rapid 1,2-hydride or alkyl shift to generate a carbon-carbon triple bond Example intermediate: C(=[C])([*:1])([H])

name: Seyferth-Gilbert Homologation
text: Hidden event (diazoalkene), seen in Seyferth-Gilbert Homologation. Trigger: Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons type olefination of a carbonyl compound using an alpha-diazomethylphosphonate Role: Spontaneously expels molecular nitrogen as a leaving group to form a vinylidene carbene Example intermediate: C(=C=[N+]=[N-])([*:1])([H])

name: Seyferth-Gilbert Homologation
text: Hidden event (oxaphosphetane), seen in Seyferth-Gilbert Homologation. Trigger: Intramolecular addition of an alkoxide oxygen to an adjacent phosphoryl group forming a four-membered ring Role: Undergoes retro-[2+2] cycloreversion to eliminate dialkyl phosphate and drive alkene formation Example intermediate: [*:2]OP1([O-])(O[*:2])C(=[N+]=[N-])C(O1)([*:1])([H])

name: Smiles Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (spirocyclic Meisenheimer complex), seen in Smiles Rearrangement. Trigger: Intramolecular attack of a tethered nucleophile (such as an amide anion) onto the ipso carbon of an aromatic ring bearing a heteroatom leaving group under basic conditions. Role: Serves as the key dearomatized intermediate that rearomatizes by cleavage of the original aryl-oxygen bond, resulting in the overall Smiles rearrangement. Example intermediate: [CH-]1C2(C=CC([*:4])=C1)OC([*:2])([*:3])C(N2[*:1])=O

name: Sommelet Reaction
text: Hidden event (iminium ion), seen in Sommelet Reaction. Trigger: Hydride transfer from a benzylic position to an electrophilic iminium or methyleneiminium acceptor Role: Undergoes nucleophilic attack by water (hydrolysis) to deliver the carbonyl product Example intermediate: [CH2]1N2CN(C[N]1C)C[N+](C2)=C([*:1])([*:2])

name: Sommelet Reaction
text: Hidden event (quaternary ammonium ion), seen in Sommelet Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic displacement of an alkyl or benzylic halide by a cage tertiary amine such as hexamethylenetetramine Role: Serves as the key covalent adduct that undergoes ring cleavage and rearrangement to initiate the redox cascade Example intermediate: C1N2CN3CN1C[N+](C([*:1])([*:2]))(C2)C3

name: Sommelet Reaction
text: Hidden event (methyleneiminium ion), seen in Sommelet Reaction. Trigger: Ring opening and fragmentation of a polycyclic quaternary ammonium species Role: Acts as an internal hydride acceptor, oxidizing the benzylic position to generate the hydrolyzable iminium intermediate Example intermediate: C1N2[CH2]N(C[N+]1=[CH2])CN(C2)C([*:1])([*:2])

name: Staudinger Reaction
text: Hidden event (iminophosphorane), seen in Staudinger Reaction. Trigger: Extrusion of dinitrogen from a triazaphosphetine intermediate formed by the reaction of a phosphine with an azide Role: Acts as a nucleophilic nitrogen ylide that readily hydrolyzes in the presence of water to furnish a primary amine and phosphine oxide, or couples with carbonyl compounds in an aza-Wittig reaction Example intermediate: [*:1]N=P([*:2])([*:3])([*:4])

name: Staudinger Reaction
text: Hidden event (triazaphosphetine), seen in Staudinger Reaction. Trigger: Intramolecular cyclization of a linear phosphazide adduct, wherein the substituted nitrogen attacks the phosphonium center to form a four-membered P-N-N-N heterocycle Role: Undergoes retro-[2+2] cycloreversion to irreversibly extrude dinitrogen gas and drive the formation of an iminophosphorane Example intermediate: [*:1]N1N=NP1([*:2])([*:3])([*:4])

name: Staudinger Reaction
text: Hidden event (phosphazide), seen in Staudinger Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic attack of a tertiary phosphine onto the terminal electrophilic nitrogen of an organic azide Role: Serves as the initial linear adduct that undergoes intramolecular cyclization into a four-membered triazaphosphetine prior to nitrogen release Example intermediate: [*:1]N=[N+]=N[P+]([*:2])([*:3])([*:4])

name: Steglich Esterification
text: Hidden event (N-acylpyridinium intermediate), seen in Steglich Esterification. Trigger: Nucleophilic attack of a 4-(dialkylamino)pyridine catalyst (e.g., DMAP) onto an activated carboxylic acid derivative such as an O-acylisourea or anhydride Role: Acts as a powerful, non-bulky acyl-transfer agent that enables nucleophilic attack by poor or sterically hindered nucleophiles while avoiding unreactive side products Example intermediate: CN(C)c1cc[n+](cc1)C(=O)[*:1]

name: Steglich Esterification
text: Hidden event (O-acylisourea intermediate), seen in Steglich Esterification. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a carboxylic acid across the central carbon of a carbodiimide coupling reagent Role: Activates the carboxylic oxygen by converting it into a potent urea leaving group susceptible to attack by DMAP or nucleophiles Example intermediate: [*:1]C(=O)OC(=[NH+][*:3])N[*:4]

name: Steglich Esterification
text: Hidden event (tetrahedral intermediate), seen in Steglich Esterification. Trigger: Nucleophilic attack of an alcohol onto an activated carbonyl species, such as an N-acylpyridinium ion Role: Collapses by eliminating the neutral pyridine catalyst to furnish the ester product Example intermediate: CN(C)c1cc[n+](cc1)C([O-])(O[*:2])[*:1]

name: Stetter Reaction
text: Hidden event (acyl anion equivalent), seen in Stetter Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a catalyst (such as cyanide or an N-heterocyclic carbene) to an aldehyde followed by deprotonation of the former formyl C-H bond. Role: Reverses the normal electrophilic polarity of the aldehyde carbon (umpolung), allowing it to act as a carbon nucleophile in conjugate addition. Example intermediate: [*:1][C-](O)C#N

name: Stetter Reaction
text: Hidden event (enolate intermediate), seen in Stetter Reaction. Trigger: Conjugate addition of a nucleophile to an α,β-unsaturated carbonyl acceptor. Role: Accepts a proton at the α-carbon to regenerate the keto form of the carbonyl acceptor. Example intermediate: [*:1]C(O)(C#N)C([*:3])C([*:4])=C([O-])[*:2]

name: Stetter Reaction
text: Hidden event (tetrahedral intermediate), seen in Stetter Reaction. Trigger: Deprotonation of the hydroxyl group in a cyanohydrin adduct, forming an alkoxide adjacent to the cyanide leaving group. Role: Collapses to reform the carbonyl C=O π-bond while expelling cyanide to achieve catalyst turnover and yield the 1,4-dicarbonyl product. Example intermediate: [*:1]C([O-])(C#N)C([*:3])C([*:4])C(=O)[*:2]

name: Stevens Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (ammonium ylide), seen in Stevens Rearrangement. Trigger: Deprotonation of a C-H bond positioned alpha to both a quaternary ammonium group and an electron-withdrawing group (such as a carbonyl) by a strong base. Role: Undergoes a 1,2-shift (via radical-pair dissociation-recombination or concerted pathway) to transfer an alkyl group from nitrogen to carbon, yielding a tertiary amine and a new C-C bond. Example intermediate: [*:1]C([O-])=C([*:2])[N+]([*:3])([*:4])[*:5]

name: Still-Gennari Reaction
text: Hidden event (oxaphosphetane), seen in Still-Gennari Reaction. Trigger: Intramolecular nucleophilic attack of an alkoxide oxygen onto a beta-phosphorus atom within a beta-alkoxyphosphonate intermediate. Role: Undergoes cycloreversion (retro-[2+2] fragmentation) to form the carbon-carbon double bond with specific stereochemical retention, releasing a phosphate byproduct. Example intermediate: [*:2]OC(=O)C1C([*:1])OP1([O-])(O[*:3])(O[*:4])

name: Still-Gennari Reaction
text: Hidden event (beta-alkoxyphosphonate), seen in Still-Gennari Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of an alpha-phosphono carbanion to the carbonyl group of an aldehyde or ketone. Role: Acts as the precursor for ring closure, positioning the alkoxide oxygen for intramolecular attack on the phosphorus atom to form the oxaphosphetane. Example intermediate: [*:2]OC(=O)C(P(=O)(O[*:3])(O[*:4]))C([O-])[*:1]

name: Still-Gennari Reaction
text: Hidden event (alpha-phosphono carbanion), seen in Still-Gennari Reaction. Trigger: Deprotonation of a phosphonate ester at the alpha position by a strong, non-nucleophilic base. Role: Acts as a resonance-stabilized carbon nucleophile that attacks the carbonyl electrophile to construct the central carbon-carbon bond. Example intermediate: [*:2]OC(=O)[CH-]P(=O)(O[*:3])(O[*:4])

name: Stobbe Condensation
text: Hidden event (gamma-lactone intermediate), seen in Stobbe Condensation. Trigger: Intramolecular nucleophilic acyl substitution of a gamma-alkoxide onto a neighboring ester carbonyl under basic conditions, followed by alkoxide expulsion Role: Temporarily locks the molecule into a cyclic scaffold, activating the alpha-proton and setting up an irreversible ring-opening elimination to form an unsaturated carboxylic acid Example intermediate: C1([*:1])([*:2])C(C(=O)O[*:3])CC(=O)O1

name: Stobbe Condensation
text: Hidden event (cyclic tetrahedral intermediate), seen in Stobbe Condensation. Trigger: Intramolecular nucleophilic addition of an alkoxide to a gamma-ester carbonyl under basic conditions Role: Collapses by ejecting an alkoxide leaving group to furnish the gamma-lactone ring Example intermediate: C1([*:1])([*:2])C(C(=O)O[*:3])CC([O-])(O[*:3])O1

name: Stobbe Condensation
text: Hidden event (lactone enolate), seen in Stobbe Condensation. Trigger: Deprotonation by base at the acidic alpha-carbon of a gamma-lactone flanked by an electron-withdrawing ester Role: Triggers E1cb ring-opening elimination with cleavage of the lactone C-O bond to generate the conjugated alkene and a carboxylate anion Example intermediate: C1([*:1])([*:2])[C-](C(=O)O[*:3])CC(=O)O1

name: Stollé Synthesis
text: Hidden event (arenium ion), seen in Stollé Synthesis. Trigger: Intramolecular electrophilic attack of an arene ring onto an activated alkyl carbon (incipient carbocation) Role: Serves as the high-energy cyclized intermediate that rearomatizes via loss of a proton to form the fused heterocyclic ring Example intermediate: C1=CC=CC2=[N+](C(CC12)=O)([*:1])

name: Stollé Synthesis
text: Hidden event (Lewis acid-alkyl halide adduct), seen in Stollé Synthesis. Trigger: Coordination of a strong Lewis acid (such as AlCl3) to the halogen atom of an alkyl halide Role: Polarizes and activates the carbon-halogen bond, generating a potent electrophilic center for electrophilic aromatic substitution Example intermediate: O=C(CCl([Al-](Cl)(Cl)Cl))N(c1ccccc1)([*:1])

name: Stork Enamine Synthesis
text: Hidden event (iminium ion), seen in Stork Enamine Synthesis. Trigger: An enamine reacts with an electrophile (such as an alkyl halide) via nucleophilic attack by the beta-carbon, driven by donation of the nitrogen lone pair. Role: Acts as an electrophilic intermediate that undergoes nucleophilic addition by water at the iminium carbon to initiate hydrolysis. Example intermediate: C([*:1])(=[N+]1CCCC1)CC([*:4])

name: Stork Enamine Synthesis
text: Hidden event (hemiaminal), seen in Stork Enamine Synthesis. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of water to an iminium ion under aqueous hydrolysis conditions. Role: Undergoes proton transfer followed by elimination of the amine leaving group to yield the ketone product. Example intermediate: C([*:1])([NH+]1CCCC1)(CC[*:4])O

name: Swern Oxidation
text: Hidden event (chlorosulfonium ion), seen in Swern Oxidation. Trigger: Activation of a dialkyl sulfoxide by an electrophilic acyl chloride at low temperature, accompanied by fragmentation and chloride addition Role: Acts as a potent sulfur electrophile that undergoes nucleophilic attack by an alcohol to form an alkoxysulfonium intermediate Example intermediate: C[S+](C)Cl

name: Swern Oxidation
text: Hidden event (alkoxysulfonium ylide), seen in Swern Oxidation. Trigger: Deprotonation of an alpha-carbon adjacent to an alkoxysulfonium center by a tertiary amine base Role: Undergoes an intramolecular cyclic elimination through a five-membered transition state to form the carbonyl group and liberate a dialkyl sulfide Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])O[S](=C)C

name: Swern Oxidation
text: Hidden event (acyloxysulfonium ion), seen in Swern Oxidation. Trigger: Nucleophilic attack of a sulfoxide oxygen onto an oxalyl or acyl chloride followed by elimination of a chloride leaving group Role: Undergoes attack by chloride at the sulfur center with concomitant fragmentation and gas evolution to generate the active halosulfonium species Example intermediate: C[S+](C)OC(=O)C(=O)Cl

name: Seyfert-Gilbert Homologation
text: Hidden event (alkylidene carbene), seen in Seyfert-Gilbert Homologation. Trigger: Extrusion of dinitrogen from a diazoalkene (or alpha-elimination from a vinyl halide/sulfoxide under basic conditions) Role: Undergoes a rapid 1,2-hydride or alkyl shift to forge an alkyne triple bond Example intermediate: [*:1]C([H])=[C]

name: Seyfert-Gilbert Homologation
text: Hidden event (1,2-oxaphosphetane), seen in Seyfert-Gilbert Homologation. Trigger: Intramolecular attack of a beta-alkoxide oxygen onto an adjacent phosphonate or phosphonium phosphorus center Role: Undergoes [2+2] cycloreversion to eliminate dialkyl phosphate (or phosphine oxide) and generate an alkene Example intermediate: [*:1]C1([H])C(P(O1)([O-])(OC)(OC))=[N+]=[N-]

name: Seyfert-Gilbert Homologation
text: Hidden event (diazoalkene), seen in Seyfert-Gilbert Homologation. Trigger: Cycloreversion of an alpha-diazo-substituted 1,2-oxaphosphetane resulting from olefination of a carbonyl Role: Extrudes molecular nitrogen as a leaving group to generate a reactive alkylidene carbene Example intermediate: [*:1]C([H])=C=[N+]=[N-]

name: Shapiro reaction
text: Hidden event (alkenyl carbanion), seen in Shapiro reaction. Trigger: Extrusion of molecular nitrogen from an alkenyldiazenide intermediate under strongly basic conditions Role: Acts as a powerful carbon nucleophile and base that undergoes protonation upon protic workup (or captures electrophiles) to form the alkene Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])=[C-][*:3]

name: Shapiro reaction
text: Hidden event (alkenyldiazenide anion), seen in Shapiro reaction. Trigger: Beta-elimination of an arenesulfinate leaving group from an alpha,N-dianionic sulfonylhydrazone Role: Spontaneously and irreversibly extrudes dinitrogen gas to generate an alkenyl carbanion Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])=C(N=[N-])[*:3]

name: Simmons-Smith Reaction
text: Hidden event (zinc carbenoid), seen in Simmons-Smith Reaction. Trigger: A gem-dihaloalkane treated with zero-valent zinc (or a Zn/Cu couple), undergoing oxidative insertion into a carbon-halogen bond. Role: Acts as a carbene equivalent, transferring a methylene group to an alkene via a stereospecific concerted transition state to yield a cyclopropane and zinc diiodide. Example intermediate: I[CH2][Zn]I

name: Takai Olefination
text: Hidden event (gem-dichromium carbenoid), seen in Takai Olefination. Trigger: A gem-polyhaloalkane reacting with an excess of a low-valent chromium(II) reagent via sequential reductions Role: Acts as a nucleophilic alkylidene equivalent that adds to a carbonyl group, forming a C-C bond while retaining a second C-metal bond Example intermediate: IC([Cr](Cl)Cl)[Cr](Cl)Cl

name: Takai Olefination
text: Hidden event (beta-chromio alkoxide), seen in Takai Olefination. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a gem-diorganometallic species to an aldehyde or ketone carbonyl group Role: Undergoes stereoselective elimination of chromium-oxygen species to generate the (E)-alkenyl halide Example intermediate: [*:1]C(O[Cr](Cl)Cl)C(I)([Cr](Cl)Cl)

name: Takai Olefination
text: Hidden event (alpha,alpha-dihaloalkylchromium intermediate), seen in Takai Olefination. Trigger: Initial single-electron transfer and halogen abstraction from a trihaloalkane by a chromium(II) salt Role: Serves as an intermediate that is further reduced by an additional equivalent of chromium(II) to yield the gem-dichromium carbenoid Example intermediate: IC(I)[Cr](Cl)Cl

name: Tebbe-Petasis Olefination
text: Hidden event (oxametallacyclobutane), seen in Tebbe-Petasis Olefination. Trigger: [2+2] cycloaddition between an electron-rich transition metal alkylidene (e.g., titanocene methylidene) and a carbonyl group Role: undergoes retro-[2+2] cycloreversion driven by the formation of a thermodynamically favorable metal-oxo double bond, yielding the alkene product Example intermediate: C1([*:1])([*:2])O[Ti]([CH2]1)(C1C=CC=C1)(C1C=CC=C1)

name: Tebbe-Petasis Olefination
text: Hidden event (transition metal alkylidene), seen in Tebbe-Petasis Olefination. Trigger: thermal alpha-elimination of an alkane from a dialkyl transition-metal complex (e.g., dimethyltitanocene) or Lewis base-mediated activation Role: acts as a nucleophilic Schrock-type carbene equivalent that engages a carbonyl electrophile in [2+2] cycloaddition Example intermediate: C=[Ti](C1C=CC=C1)(C1C=CC=C1)

name: Thorpe-Ziegler Reaction
text: Hidden event (ketiminyl anion), seen in Thorpe-Ziegler Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a carbanion to a nitrile group under basic conditions Role: Undergoes protonation at the nitrogen atom to form a neutral imine intermediate that can tautomerize to an enamine Example intermediate: N#CC1C(=[N-])C[*:1]C1

name: Thorpe-Ziegler Reaction
text: Hidden event (alpha-cyano carbanion), seen in Thorpe-Ziegler Reaction. Trigger: Deprotonation of a carbon atom alpha to a nitrile group by a strong base Role: Acts as a carbon nucleophile to attack an electrophilic center, such as an intramolecular cyano group, forging a new carbon-carbon bond Example intermediate: N#C[C-][CH2][*:1][CH2]C#N

name: Thorpe-Ziegler Reaction
text: Hidden event (beta-iminonitrile), seen in Thorpe-Ziegler Reaction. Trigger: Protonation of the ketiminyl anion formed upon addition of an alpha-cyano carbanion to a nitrile Role: Undergoes base-mediated tautomerization via alpha-deprotonation and nitrogen reprotonation to deliver the conjugated beta-enaminonitrile product Example intermediate: N#CC1C(=N)C[*:1]C1

name: Tiffeneau–Demjanov rearrangement
text: Hidden event (alkyldiazonium ion), seen in Tiffeneau–Demjanov rearrangement. Trigger: Primary aliphatic amine undergoing diazotization with nitrous acid under acidic conditions Role: Extrudes molecular nitrogen as an exceptionally good leaving group, triggering a concerted or carbocationic 1,2-alkyl shift assisted by the adjacent hydroxyl group Example intermediate: N#[N+]C([*:3])([*:4])C(O)([*:1])([*:2])

name: Tiffeneau–Demjanov rearrangement
text: Hidden event (oxocarbenium ion), seen in Tiffeneau–Demjanov rearrangement. Trigger: 1,2-migration of an alkyl or aryl group onto a developing carbocationic center with lone-pair assistance from a neighboring hydroxyl group Role: Acts as the protonated form of the rearranged carbonyl compound, undergoing facile deprotonation to deliver the neutral ketone or aldehyde product Example intermediate: [OH+]=C([*:1])C([*:2])([*:3])([*:4])

name: Tiffeneau–Demjanov rearrangement
text: Hidden event (nitrosonium ion), seen in Tiffeneau–Demjanov rearrangement. Trigger: Protonation of nitrous acid under acidic conditions followed by loss of water Role: Serves as the key electrophile that nitrosates the primary amino group to initiate the diazotization sequence Example intermediate: N#[O+]

name: Tollens Oxidation
text: Hidden event (alkoxyl radical), seen in Tollens Oxidation. Trigger: Homolytic cleavage of a metal-oxygen bond following single-electron reduction of a coordinated redox-active metal center (such as Ag(I) to Ag(0)) in a metal alkoxide or diolate complex Role: Undergoes an intramolecular 1,2-hydrogen atom shift from the alpha carbon to the oxygen radical to form a more stable carbon-centered radical Example intermediate: [O]C(O([Ag](N)(N)))[*:1]

name: Tollens Oxidation
text: Hidden event (alpha-hydroxyalkyl radical), seen in Tollens Oxidation. Trigger: 1,2-hydrogen atom transfer from an aldehyde-derived hydrate carbon to an adjacent alkoxyl radical Role: Undergoes a second single-electron transfer and homolytic fragmentation of the remaining metal-oxygen bond to deliver the carboxylic acid product and metallic silver Example intermediate: O[C](O([Ag](N)(N)))[*:1]

name: Tollens Oxidation
text: Hidden event (metal alkoxide adduct), seen in Tollens Oxidation. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of water to a carbonyl group in the presence of a coordinating, redox-active transition metal cation under basic aqueous conditions Role: Binds the oxidant directly to the substrate oxygens, positioning the system for single-electron transfer and homolytic metal-oxygen cleavage Example intermediate: O([Ag](N)(N))C(O([Ag](N)(N)))[*:1]

name: Trost Asymmetric Allylation Alkylation
text: Hidden event (allylpalladium complex), seen in Trost Asymmetric Allylation Alkylation. Trigger: An allylic substrate containing a leaving group undergoes oxidative addition or ionization upon coordination to a palladium(0) catalyst bearing chiral or achiral ligands. Role: Serves as an electrophilic species that is attacked at one of the allyl termini by a stabilized nucleophile, defining the regiochemical and stereochemical outcome of the reaction. Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])=C([*:3])C([Pd]([*:6])([*:7])([*:7]))([*:4])([*:5])

name: Trost Asymmetric Allylation Alkylation
text: Hidden event (palladium-alkene pi-complex), seen in Trost Asymmetric Allylation Alkylation. Trigger: Nucleophilic attack on an allylpalladium intermediate generates a newly formed C-C bond while the resulting alkene remains datively coordinated to the reduced palladium center. Role: Undergoes olefin dissociation to release the final allylic substitution product and regenerate the active palladium(0) catalyst for further catalytic cycles. Example intermediate: COC(=O)C(C(=O)OC)C([*:4])([*:5])/C1([*:3])[Pd]([*:7])([*:7])C1([*:2])([*:1])

name: Tsuji-Trost Reaction
text: Hidden event (allylpalladium complex), seen in Tsuji-Trost Reaction. Trigger: An allylic compound bearing a leaving group undergoes oxidative addition with a low-valent palladium catalyst in the presence of coordinating ligands. Role: Acts as an electrophile that undergoes nucleophilic attack at the allylic terminus, establishing the new carbon-carbon or carbon-heteroatom bond. Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])=C([*:3])C([Pd]([*:6])([*:7])([*:7]))([*:4])([*:5])

name: Tsuji-Trost Reaction
text: Hidden event (alkene-palladium complex), seen in Tsuji-Trost Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition to an allylpalladium complex, which forms the substituted allylic bond while the resulting olefin remains coordinated to the reduced palladium(0) center. Role: Undergoes olefin dissociation to liberate the final allylic substitution product and regenerate the active palladium(0) catalyst. Example intermediate: N#CC(C#N)C([*:4])([*:5])/C1([*:3])[Pd]([*:7])([*:7])C1([*:2])([*:1])

name: Ugi Reaction
text: Hidden event (nitrilium ion), seen in Ugi Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of an isocyanide carbon to an electrophilic iminium species Role: Acts as an exceptionally reactive electrophile that is rapidly trapped by a carboxylate nucleophile Example intermediate: [*:2]NC([*:3])([*:4])C#[N+][*:5]

name: Ugi Reaction
text: Hidden event (imidoyl carboxylate), seen in Ugi Reaction. Trigger: Addition of a carboxylic acid or carboxylate to an electrophilic nitrilium intermediate Role: Acts as an activated mixed anhydride equivalent, positioning the acyl group for an intramolecular O-to-N Mumm acyl transfer Example intermediate: [*:2]NC([*:3])([*:4])C(OC(=[OH+])[*:1])=N[*:5]

name: Ugi Reaction
text: Hidden event (cyclic Mumm intermediate), seen in Ugi Reaction. Trigger: Intramolecular nucleophilic attack of a proximal amine onto the acyl carbon of an imidoyl carboxylate Role: Undergoes heterocyclic C-O bond cleavage to effect irreversible O-to-N acyl transfer, driving the reaction to the stable bis-amide product Example intermediate: [*:2][NH+]1C([*:3])([*:4])C(=N[*:5])OC1(O)[*:1]

name: Ullmann Condensation
text: Hidden event (arylcopper(III) dihalide complex), seen in Ullmann Condensation. Trigger: Oxidative addition of an aryl halide to a copper(I) catalyst under basic conditions Role: Provides an electrophilic metal center that undergoes ligand exchange with a heteroatom nucleophile to displace a halide Example intermediate: c1([*:6])c([*:7])c([*:8])c([*:9])c([*:10])c1[Cu](I)I

name: Ullmann Condensation
text: Hidden event (aryl(aryloxy)copper(III) complex), seen in Ullmann Condensation. Trigger: Ligand exchange/nucleophilic displacement of a halide on an arylcopper(III) intermediate by a phenolate Role: Undergoes reductive elimination to forge the aryl carbon-oxygen bond and regenerate the active copper(I) catalyst Example intermediate: c2([*:6])c([*:7])c([*:8])c([*:9])c([*:10])c2[Cu](I)Oc1c([*:1])c([*:2])c([*:3])c([*:4])c1([*:5])

name: Ullmann Coupling
text: Hidden event (diarylcopper(III) intermediate), seen in Ullmann Coupling. Trigger: Oxidative addition of an aryl halide to an arylcopper(I) species under copper-promoted cross-coupling conditions Role: Undergoes rapid reductive elimination to forge the new biaryl C(sp2)-C(sp2) bond and eliminate copper(I) iodide Example intermediate: c1([*:1])c([*:2])c([*:3])c([*:4])c([*:5])c1[Cu](I)c2c([*:1])c([*:2])c([*:3])c([*:4])c2([*:5])

name: Ullmann Coupling
text: Hidden event (organocopper(I) intermediate), seen in Ullmann Coupling. Trigger: Single-electron reduction of an arylcopper(II) halide species in the presence of copper metal Role: Acts as the nucleophilic organometallic intermediate that oxidatively adds a second molecule of aryl halide Example intermediate: c1([*:1])c([*:2])c([*:3])c([*:4])c([*:5])c1[Cu]

name: Ullmann Coupling
text: Hidden event (organocopper(II) halide complex), seen in Ullmann Coupling. Trigger: Initial oxidative addition or halogen-atom transfer between an aryl halide and metallic copper Role: Undergoes single-electron transfer reduction to furnish the active arylcopper(I) coupling species Example intermediate: c1([*:1])c([*:2])c([*:3])c([*:4])c([*:5])c1[Cu]I

name: Upjohn Dihydroxylation
text: Hidden event (cyclic osmate(VI) ester), seen in Upjohn Dihydroxylation. Trigger: An alkene reacting with osmium tetroxide (OsO4) via concerted [3+2] cycloaddition in the presence of water and a stoichiometric co-oxidant such as NMO. Role: Hydrolyzes to release the syn-1,2-diol, dictating the cis-stereospecificity of the dihydroxylation, while liberating a reduced osmium(VI) species for reoxidation. Example intermediate: C1([*:1])([*:2])O[Os](=O)(=O)OC1([*:3])([*:4])

name: Van Leusen Reaction
text: Hidden event (dihydrooxazolyl anion), seen in Van Leusen Reaction. Trigger: Intramolecular nucleophilic addition of a β-alkoxide onto an adjacent isocyanide carbon under basic conditions, typically following addition of an α-isocyano carbanion to a carbonyl. Role: Forms a transient five-membered heterocyclic ring that activates the scaffold for deprotonation and subsequent cascade ring-opening elimination. Example intermediate: Cc1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)C1N=[C-]OC1([*:1])([*:2])

name: Van Leusen Reaction
text: Hidden event (N-formylketenimine), seen in Van Leusen Reaction. Trigger: Base-promoted ring-opening and elimination of an arylsulfinate leaving group from a 4-arylsulfonyl-4,5-dihydrooxazole. Role: Acts as an activated cumulated intermediate bearing an electrophilic formyl group, rendering it susceptible to nucleophilic deformylation to access the nitrile. Example intermediate: C(=C=NC=O)([*:1])([*:2])

name: Van Leusen Reaction
text: Hidden event (tetrahedral addition intermediate), seen in Van Leusen Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of an alkoxide to the carbonyl carbon of an N-acyl- or N-formylketenimine. Role: Collapses via carbon-nitrogen bond cleavage to expel the keteniminyl anion with loss of an alkyl formate byproduct, completing net deformylation. Example intermediate: C(=C=NC([O-])OC(C)(C)C)([*:1])([*:2])

name: Vilsmeier-Haack Formylation
text: Hidden event (chloroiminium ion), seen in Vilsmeier-Haack Formylation. Trigger: Reaction of a tertiary formamide or amide with an activating chlorinating reagent such as phosphorus oxychloride, oxalyl chloride, or thionyl chloride Role: Acts as the active, highly reactive carbon electrophile that undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution with electron-rich pi-systems Example intermediate: ClC(=[N+](C)C)

name: Vilsmeier-Haack Formylation
text: Hidden event (arenium ion), seen in Vilsmeier-Haack Formylation. Trigger: Electrophilic addition of a potent electrophile to an electron-rich aromatic ring, temporarily disrupting aromaticity Role: Undergoes rapid deprotonation to restore aromatic resonance energy, establishing the new carbon-carbon bond Example intermediate: c1([*:5])c([*:4])c([*:3])c([*:2])[C+]([*:1])C1C(Cl)N(C)C

name: Vilsmeier-Haack Formylation
text: Hidden event (iminium ion), seen in Vilsmeier-Haack Formylation. Trigger: Expulsion of chloride from an alpha-chloroalkylamine driven by the nitrogen lone pair Role: Persists as the precursor salt until aqueous workup, where it undergoes nucleophilic addition of water followed by secondary amine elimination to yield the carbonyl product Example intermediate: C(=[N+](C)C)c1c([*:1])c([*:2])c([*:3])c([*:4])c1[*:5]

name: Weinreb Ketone Synthesis
text: Hidden event (chelated tetrahedral intermediate), seen in Weinreb Ketone Synthesis. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of an organomagnesium or organolithium reagent to a Weinreb amide (N-methoxy-N-methylamide), where the metal cation coordinates simultaneously to the newly generated alkoxide oxygen and the methoxy oxygen. Role: Prevents premature collapse of the tetrahedral intermediate to the ketone under the reaction conditions, avoiding overaddition of the organometallic nucleophile until aqueous quench. Example intermediate: [*:1]C([*:2])(O[Mg-]1(Br))N(C)[O+]1C

name: Weinreb Ketone Synthesis
text: Hidden event (hemiaminal intermediate), seen in Weinreb Ketone Synthesis. Trigger: Aqueous protonation and decomplexation of the metal-chelated Weinreb tetrahedral adduct upon workup. Role: Serves as the unchelated tetrahedral species that undergoes protonation and subsequent elimination of the N-methoxy-N-methylamino group to generate the ketone product. Example intermediate: C([*:1])(O)([*:2])N(C)OC

name: Weiss-Cook Condensation
text: Hidden event (cyclopentadienone), seen in Weiss-Cook Condensation. Trigger: Dual aldol condensation and dehydration of a 1,3-dicarbonyl compound with a 1,2-dicarbonyl compound under basic conditions. Role: Acts as an exceptionally reactive, electron-deficient cyclic diene/enone that rapidly undergoes intermolecular conjugate addition with a second enolate rather than dimerizing, advancing the cascade annulation. Example intermediate: [*:1]OC(=O)C1C(=O)C(=CC=1)C(=O)O[*:1]

name: Weiss-Cook Condensation
text: Hidden event (cyclopentenone), seen in Weiss-Cook Condensation. Trigger: Conjugate addition of a stabilized carbanion (such as a 1,3-dicarbonyl enolate) to a cyclopentadienone under basic conditions. Role: Acts as an electrophilic acceptor for an intramolecular conjugate addition by the pendant enolate, forging the second five-membered ring to construct the bicyclo[3.3.0]octane framework. Example intermediate: [*:1]OC(=O)C1C(=O)C(=CC1(CC(=O)C(C(=O)O[*:1])C(=O)O[*:1]))C(=O)O[*:1]

name: Weiss-Cook Condensation
text: Hidden event (alpha,beta-unsaturated aldehyde), seen in Weiss-Cook Condensation. Trigger: Intermolecular aldol/Knoevenagel condensation between a 1,3-dicarbonyl compound and one carbonyl group of an alpha-dicarbonyl compound under basic conditions with elimination of water. Role: Positions the unreacted aldehyde carbonyl for intramolecular nucleophilic attack by the remaining enolizable alpha-position to close the first five-membered ring. Example intermediate: [*:1]OC(=O)CC(=O)C(=CC=O)C(=O)O[*:1]

name: Wharton Reaction
text: Hidden event (alkenyl diazene), seen in Wharton Reaction. Trigger: Epoxide ring opening of an alpha,beta-epoxy hydrazone driven by the terminal nitrogen lone pair, followed by deprotonation Role: Undergoes fragmentation with loss of molecular nitrogen to form a carbanion Example intermediate: N=NC([*:1])=C([*:2])C(O)([*:3])[*:4]

name: Wharton Reaction
text: Hidden event (vinyl carbanion), seen in Wharton Reaction. Trigger: Spontaneous or base-promoted extrusion of dinitrogen from an alkenyl diazene Role: Undergoes rapid protonation from solvent or an acid source to establish the newly formed alkene Example intermediate: [C-](=C([*:2])C(O)([*:3])[*:4])[*:1]

name: Wharton Reaction
text: Hidden event (alpha,beta-epoxy hydrazone), seen in Wharton Reaction. Trigger: Condensation of an alpha,beta-epoxy ketone with hydrazine under mildly acidic or neutral conditions Role: Serves as the key covalent adduct whose nitrogen lone pair promotes opening of the adjacent strained oxirane ring Example intermediate: C(=NN)([*:1])C1([*:2])OC1([*:3])[*:4]

name: Willgerodt-Kindler Reaction
text: Hidden event (aziridinium ion), seen in Willgerodt-Kindler Reaction. Trigger: A secondary amine positioned beta to an electrophilic carbon (such as a thionium intermediate) under thermal conditions Role: Enables 1,2-migration of the amino group along the carbon chain through intramolecular ring formation and subsequent regioselective ring opening Example intermediate: [N+]([*:6])([*:7])2C(c1c([*:1])c([*:2])c([*:3])c([*:4])c1([*:5]))C2SSSSSSSS

name: Willgerodt-Kindler Reaction
text: Hidden event (enamine), seen in Willgerodt-Kindler Reaction. Trigger: Condensation of an enolizable carbonyl compound with a secondary amine under heating Role: Serves as an activated carbon nucleophile to attack elemental sulfur at the alpha position, initiating carbon-sulfur bond formation Example intermediate: C=C(N([*:6])([*:7]))c1c([*:1])c([*:2])c([*:3])c([*:4])c1([*:5])

name: Willgerodt-Kindler Reaction
text: Hidden event (thionium ion), seen in Willgerodt-Kindler Reaction. Trigger: Tautomerization or proton transfer of an alpha-sulfanyl enamine into a sulfur-stabilized carbocation Role: Acts as an electrophilic acceptor that undergoes intramolecular attack by the neighboring amine nitrogen to forge the aziridinium ring Example intermediate: N([*:6])([*:7])C(c1c([*:1])c([*:2])c([*:3])c([*:4])c1([*:5]))C=[S+]SSSSSSSS

name: Wittig Reaction
text: Hidden event (oxaphosphetane), seen in Wittig Reaction. Trigger: Formal [2+2] cycloaddition of a phosphorus ylide with a carbonyl group (aldehyde or ketone) Role: Undergoes a [2+2] cycloreversion driven by the thermodynamic formation of a strong phosphorus-oxygen double bond, yielding the alkene product and phosphine oxide Example intermediate: c1ccccc1P1(c2ccccc2)(c2ccccc2)OC([*:3])([*:4])C1([*:1])[*:2]

name: Wittig Reaction
text: Hidden event (phosphonium ylide), seen in Wittig Reaction. Trigger: Deprotonation of an alkylphosphonium salt at the alpha-carbon by a strong base Role: Serves as a carbanionic nucleophile that adds to an electrophilic carbonyl compound to form the four-membered oxaphosphetane ring Example intermediate: c1ccccc1[P+](c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)[C-]([*:1])[*:2]

name: Wittig Rearrangement-[2,3]
text: Hidden event (alpha-alkoxy carbanion), seen in Wittig Rearrangement-[2,3]. Trigger: Deprotonation of an allyl ether at the position alpha to the ether oxygen using a strong organolithium base. Role: Acts as the migrating carbanionic component in a concerted, suprafacial [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement via a five-membered envelope transition state to form a new C-C bond with allylic transposition. Example intermediate: C([*:1])([*:2])=C([*:3])C([*:4])([*:5])O[CH-][*:6]

name: Wohl-Ziegler Reaction
text: Hidden event (allylic radical), seen in Wohl-Ziegler Reaction. Trigger: An alkene possessing an allylic C-H bond exposed to a halogen radical under thermal or photochemical radical conditions in a nonpolar solvent Role: Delocalizes the radical across the conjugated pi system and abstracts a bromine atom to furnish the allylic bromide product while regenerating the chain carrier Example intermediate: [*:1]C([*:2])=C([*:3])[C]([*:4])[*:5]

name: Wohl-Ziegler Reaction
text: Hidden event (bromine radical), seen in Wohl-Ziegler Reaction. Trigger: An N-bromoimide or molecular bromine undergoing homolytic cleavage or halogen atom transfer with an initiating radical under heat or light Role: Propagates the radical chain by selectively abstracting a weak allylic hydrogen atom to form hydrogen bromide and the resonance-stabilized allylic radical Example intermediate: [Br]

name: Wohl-Ziegler Reaction
text: Hidden event (alkyl radical), seen in Wohl-Ziegler Reaction. Trigger: An aliphatic azo compound subjected to heat or photochemical irradiation undergoing extrusion of dinitrogen Role: Initiates the radical chain mechanism by abstracting a halogen atom from the halogen source to generate the propagating halogen radical Example intermediate: C[C](C)C#N

name: Wolff-Kishner Reduction
text: Hidden event (carbanion), seen in Wolff-Kishner Reduction. Trigger: Extrusion of dinitrogen gas from an alkyldiazene intermediate under strongly basic, high-temperature conditions Role: Rapidly abstracts a proton from the protic solvent to yield the fully reduced hydrocarbon product Example intermediate: [CH-]([*:1])[*:2]

name: Wolff-Kishner Reduction
text: Hidden event (alkyldiazene), seen in Wolff-Kishner Reduction. Trigger: Base-promoted tautomerization of a hydrazone via deprotonation at nitrogen and subsequent protonation at carbon Role: Undergoes elimination to irreversibly extrude molecular nitrogen and generate an unstabilized carbanion Example intermediate: C(N=N)([*:1])[*:2]

name: Wolff-Kishner Reduction
text: Hidden event (hydrazone), seen in Wolff-Kishner Reduction. Trigger: Condensation of an aldehyde or ketone carbonyl with hydrazine under thermal conditions Role: Serves as the key covalent adduct that undergoes base-mediated tautomerization to an alkyldiazene intermediate Example intermediate: C(=NN)([*:1])[*:2]

name: Wolff Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (acylcarbene), seen in Wolff Rearrangement. Trigger: Thermolysis, photolysis, or transition metal-catalyzed activation of an alpha-diazocarbonyl compound leading to extrusion of dinitrogen Role: Undergoes a rapid 1,2-migratory shift of an adjacent substituent to the electron-deficient carbene carbon with concomitant pi-bond formation to yield a ketene Example intermediate: C([*:1])(=O)[C][*:2]

name: Yamaguchi Esterification
text: Hidden event (mixed anhydride), seen in Yamaguchi Esterification. Trigger: Reaction of a carboxylic acid with a sterically hindered or electron-deficient acid chloride (such as 2,4,6-trichlorobenzoyl chloride) in the presence of a tertiary amine base. Role: Activates the carboxylic acid toward nucleophilic acyl substitution while providing steric differentiation that directs nucleophilic attack selectively to the desired carbonyl. Example intermediate: C(=O)(OC(=O)c1c(Cl)cc(Cl)cc1Cl)[*:1]

name: Yamaguchi Esterification
text: Hidden event (N-acylpyridinium intermediate), seen in Yamaguchi Esterification. Trigger: Nucleophilic attack of a 4-dialkylaminopyridine catalyst (such as DMAP) onto an activated carboxylic acid derivative, displacing a carboxylate or halide leaving group. Role: Acts as a potent, electrophilic catalyst-bound acylating agent that accelerates acyl transfer to weak nucleophiles (e.g., hindered alcohols) and regenerates the catalyst. Example intermediate: C(=O)([n+]1ccc(N(C)C)cc1)[*:1]

name: Yamaguchi Esterification
text: Hidden event (tetrahedral intermediate), seen in Yamaguchi Esterification. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of a heteroatom nucleophile (such as an amine catalyst, alcohol, or carboxylate) to an activated carbonyl carbon. Role: Temporarily accommodates the newly formed bond and negative charge on oxygen before collapsing to eliminate a leaving group and restore the carbonyl. Example intermediate: C([O-])(OC(=O)c1c(Cl)cc(Cl)cc1Cl)([n+]1ccc(N(C)C)cc1)[*:1]

name: Zincke Reaction
text: Hidden event (1,2-dihydropyridine), seen in Zincke Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic addition of an amine to the electron-deficient 2-position of an N-activated (e.g., N-dinitrophenyl) pyridinium salt under polar conditions. Role: Undergoes electrocyclic ring opening (retro-6π electrocyclization) to cleave the heterocyclic ring and yield an acyclic conjugated polyene imine. Example intermediate: [*:1]N([*:2])C1C=CC=CN1(c1cc(cc(c1)[N+]([O-])=O)[N+]([O-])=O)

name: Zincke Reaction
text: Hidden event (conjugated imine), seen in Zincke Reaction. Trigger: Spontaneous 6π electrocyclic ring opening of a 1,2-dihydropyridine bearing an electron-withdrawing substituent on the nitrogen atom. Role: Undergoes nucleophilic attack by water (hydrolysis) at the terminal imine carbon to displace the aryl amine leaving group, delivering the open-chain Zincke aldehyde product. Example intermediate: [*:1]N([*:2])C=CC=CC=N(c1cc(cc(c1)[N+]([O-])=O)[N+]([O-])=O)

name: Ramberg-Bäcklund Reaction
text: Hidden event (thiirane 1,1-dioxide), seen in Ramberg-Bäcklund Reaction. Trigger: An alpha-haloalkyl sulfone (bearing an alpha-leaving group and an alpha'-hydrogen) treated with a strong base, leading to alpha'-deprotonation and subsequent intramolecular nucleophilic substitution (cyclization). Role: Undergoes cheletropic extrusion of sulfur dioxide (SO2), cleaving both carbon-sulfur bonds to establish the C=C double bond of the alkene product. Example intermediate: C1([*:1])([*:2])S(=O)(=O)C1([*:3])[*:4]

name: Rauhut-Currier Reaction
text: Hidden event (phosphonium enolate), seen in Rauhut-Currier Reaction. Trigger: Conjugate addition of a nucleophilic phosphine catalyst to an electron-deficient alkene (Michael acceptor) Role: Acts as an umpolung carbon nucleophile to attack a second electron-deficient alkene in a conjugate addition, forging a key carbon–carbon bond Example intermediate: [*:1]C([O-])=CC([*:2])([*:3])[P+]([*:8])([*:8])[*:8]

name: Rauhut-Currier Reaction
text: Hidden event (zwitterionic Michael adduct), seen in Rauhut-Currier Reaction. Trigger: Conjugate addition of a catalyst-derived enolate (such as a phosphonium enolate) to an activated alkene (Michael acceptor) Role: Represents the initial carbon–carbon coupled adduct that undergoes tautomerization to set up the beta-elimination of the phosphine catalyst Example intermediate: [*:1]C(=O)C(C([*:2])([*:3])([P+]([*:8])([*:8])[*:8]))C([*:4])([*:5])C([*:6])=C([O-])[*:7]

name: Reformatsky Reaction
text: Hidden event (organozinc halide), seen in Reformatsky Reaction. Trigger: Oxidative insertion of zinc metal into an alpha-halo ester C-halogen bond Role: Serves as a mild, stabilized carbanion equivalent that selectively adds to aldehyde or ketone electrophiles while resisting self-condensation with ester carbonyls Example intermediate: [*:1]OC(=O)C([*:2])([*:3])[Zn]Br

name: Reformatsky Reaction
text: Hidden event (zinc alkoxide), seen in Reformatsky Reaction. Trigger: Nucleophilic attack of a carbon-zinc nucleophile onto an aldehyde or ketone carbonyl group Role: Stores the tetrahedral addition product as a stable metal alkoxide until aqueous acidic quench hydrolyzes the zinc-oxygen bond to yield the beta-hydroxy ester Example intermediate: C(C([O-])([*:4])[*:5])([*:2])([*:3])C(=O)O[*:1].[Zn+2].[Br-]

name: Reimer-Tiemann Formylation
text: Hidden event (dihalocarbene), seen in Reimer-Tiemann Formylation. Trigger: Deprotonation of a trihalomethane by a strong base followed by alpha-elimination of a halide leaving group Role: Acts as an electron-deficient, neutral carbon electrophile that attacks electron-rich pi-systems such as phenolates Example intermediate: [C](Cl)Cl

name: Reimer-Tiemann Formylation
text: Hidden event (ortho-quinone methide), seen in Reimer-Tiemann Formylation. Trigger: Expulsion of a leaving group from an ortho-(alpha-haloalkyl)phenolate driven by the phenolate oxygen lone pair Role: Serves as a reactive conjugated electrophile that rapidly undergoes nucleophilic attack (e.g., hydration by hydroxide) at the exocyclic carbon Example intermediate: C1(=O)C(=CCl)C([*:4])=C([*:3])C([*:2])=C1([*:1])

name: Reimer-Tiemann Formylation
text: Hidden event (dearomatized cyclohexadienone carbanion), seen in Reimer-Tiemann Formylation. Trigger: Addition of an electron-rich phenolate ring carbon to a neutral carbene electrophile Role: Traps a proton from the ring sp3 position to restore aromatic stabilization Example intermediate: C1(=O)C([C-](Cl)Cl)C([*:1])=C([*:2])C([*:3])=C1([*:4])

name: Rieche Formylation
text: Hidden event (oxocarbenium ion), seen in Rieche Formylation. Trigger: Reaction of an alpha-halo ether or gem-dihalo ether with a strong Lewis acid, resulting in halide abstraction. Role: Acts as the key electrophilic species that undergoes electrophilic addition to the aromatic ring. Example intermediate: C[O+]=CCl

name: Rieche Formylation
text: Hidden event (arenium ion), seen in Rieche Formylation. Trigger: Electrophilic addition of a reactive cationic species to an aromatic ring, disrupting aromaticity. Trigger: Beta-elimination of an adjacent proton from a propargylic carbocation in an alkynyl alcohol derivative Role: Serves as the key neutral intermediate that undergoes regioselective electrophilic protonation at the alkyne terminus Example intermediate: C#CC(=C(Br)OC)c1ccc(OC)cc1

name: Rupe Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (vinyl cation), seen in Rupe Rearrangement. Trigger: Conjugated enyne subjected to strong acid, undergoing electrophilic addition of a proton to the terminal alkyne carbon Role: Traps water nucleophilically at the internal carbon to form an enol intermediate that tautomerizes to the conjugated enone product Example intermediate: C=[C+]C(=C(Br)OC)c1ccc(OC)cc1

name: Rupe Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (propargylic carbocation), seen in Rupe Rearrangement. Trigger: A propargylic alcohol bearing beta-hydrogens is treated with a strong acid, leading to hydroxyl protonation and heterolytic cleavage with loss of water. Role: Undergoes E1-type elimination of a beta-hydrogen to form a conjugated 1,3-enyne rather than undergoing 1,3-transposition. Example intermediate: C#C[C+](c1ccc(OC)cc1)C(C(=O)C)F

name: Rupe Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (1,3-enyne), seen in Rupe Rearrangement. Trigger: Acid-promoted dehydration (beta-elimination) of a propargylic alcohol containing an adjacent aliphatic C-H bond. Role: Serves as the key conjugated intermediate whose terminal alkyne moiety undergoes regioselective electrophilic protonation and hydration to afford an alpha,beta-unsaturated ketone. Example intermediate: C#CC(=C(C(=O)C)F)c1ccc(OC)cc1

name: Rupe Rearrangement
text: Hidden event (vinyl carbocation), seen in Rupe Rearrangement. Trigger: Electrophilic addition of a proton to the terminal carbon of an alkyne or conjugated enyne under acidic conditions. Role: Acts as a potent electrophile that captures water via nucleophilic addition to deliver the hydrated enol intermediate. Example intermediate: C=[C+]C(=C(C(=O)C)F)c1ccc(OC)cc1
